0.name: The gold eight-pointed star
0.seen: High in the upper right, a large eight-pointed star is inlaid in gold against the lapis night, far brighter than the scattered pyrite flecks around it. The Fool’s face is tipped straight towards it.

0.name: Two swallows among clouds
0.seen: Two small birds with long, pointed wings glide through the upper left of the sky between low bands of cloud. They are carved in the pale grey-blue of the lapis itself, not in ivory.

0.name: The upturned face
0.seen: The Fool’s ivory head is tipped back in profile, wavy hair falling to the nape, eyes lifted towards the gold star. The gaze never drops to the rim a short step ahead.

0.name: The bundle on the staff
0.seen: The forward hand grips a slender ivory staff slanting up to the right. Near its tip hangs a small, soft cloth bundle, cinched at the neck with a knotted bow.

0.name: The white rose
0.seen: In the trailing hand, held low beside the wind-pulled robe, the Fool carries a single open ivory rose on a short stem with a few small leaves.

0.name: The crescent and starry orb
0.seen: On the rocky ground behind the Fool, at left, a pale silvery crescent cradles a disc of lapis set with small gold stars. Just above it, to the right, hangs an ivory sphere dotted with gold stars.

0.name: The leaping white dog
0.seen: An ivory dog springs past the Fool’s leading leg in mid-leap, forepaws already out beyond the rim of the cliff, tail streaming behind, mouth open, head raised the same way as the traveller.

0.name: The lapis cliff edge
0.seen: The Fool strides barefoot across a flat-topped outcrop of lighter, veined lapis that breaks off in a sheer carved face to the right, the leading foot planted just short of the rim. Blue peaks rise far behind on the left.

0.name: The lily below the cliff
0.seen: At the lower right, beneath the drop, a tall lily is carved in pale grey-blue with long, blade-like leaves, growing among grasses at the edge of a still, shallow pool.

1.name: The glittering Milky Way
1.seen: A diagonal band of fine silvery sparkle runs from the top edge down to the left edge of the night sky, passing just beside the tip of the raised wand. It is far denser than the scattered gold star flecks.

1.name: The raised ivory wand
1.seen: The figure’s right arm, on the viewer’s left, reaches up and out above the head, the fingers closed around a slender ivory rod held nearly upright, with a small grooved knob at its top end.

1.name: The gold lemniscate
1.seen: Above the head floats a horizontal figure of eight inlaid in gold, two smooth closed loops crossing at the centre. It is the largest piece of gold on the card, set against the pale blue field behind the figure.

1.name: The ivory robe and mantle
1.seen: A plain round-necked tunic under a heavy mantle draped over both shoulders, gathered in deep folds at the raised arm and falling in long folds behind the table. Both are carved in the same warm ivory.

1.name: The serpent girdle
1.seen: A scaled serpent carved in grey-blue lapis circles the waist as a belt and crosses over itself in a loop at the front. Its head rests on top of the loop, facing the viewer’s left, mouth closed.

1.name: The mountains and water
1.seen: Behind the table on the left, a pale mountain range rises beyond a wide stretch of still water marked with fine horizontal lines, all carved in shallow relief in a lighter, greyer blue.

1.name: The hand pointing down
1.seen: The figure’s left arm, on the viewer’s right, extends down and outwards from the mantle. The index finger points firmly down towards the carved flowers at the foot of the card, the other fingers curled in.

1.name: The four tools on the table
1.seen: On a heavy lapis table with a moulded base stand, from left: a stemmed cup, a sword upright on its pommel with the point to the sky, a slim rod ending in a round knob, and a disc bearing a five-pointed star.

1.name: Roses and lilies below
1.seen: Along the foot of the card, in front of the table, open roses, rosebuds and star-shaped lilies grow together among leaves, all carved in grey-blue lapis rather than ivory or red.

2.name: The horned crown and gold disc
2.seen: Two smooth ivory horns curve upward from a band across the veiled brow and cradle a round disc of textured gold, the only gold on the figure itself; elsewhere gold appears only as scattered flecks in the stone.

2.name: The closed eyes
2.seen: Beneath the crown the ivory face is calm and slightly lowered, eyelids closed, mouth at rest. A plain veil falls from the head band over both shoulders and down past the elbows.

2.name: The pomegranate veil
2.seen: Behind the figure hangs a lapis cloth gathered in swags along its upper rod, carved in low relief with round, crowned pomegranates and curling vines. Above it, a recessed arch opens onto gold-flecked night.

2.name: The dark pillar
2.seen: On the viewer’s left stands a column of deep ultramarine lapis with a rough, pitted shaft, a leafy capital with curled corner volutes and a stepped base. No letter is carved on it.

2.name: The pale pillar
2.seen: On the viewer’s right rises its twin in pale, cloudy blue lapis, polished smooth and faintly veined, with the same leafy capital and stepped base, in clearly lighter stone than its partner.

2.name: The round clasp
2.seen: At the gathered neckline of the ivory gown, where fine pleats radiate outward, sits a small, smooth round boss like a clasp or a pearl. A narrow sash circles the high waist below.

2.name: The closed tablet in the lap
2.seen: Both ivory hands lie flat and relaxed in the lap, fingers loose, resting on a small closed rectangle like a book or tablet whose edge shows beneath the hand on the viewer’s left.

2.name: The scroll set aside
2.seen: Beside the knee on the viewer’s right, an ivory scroll rests upright against the gown and seat, its top rolled into a tight curl, its open length hanging towards the floor, faintly incised with lines of indistinct script.

2.name: The crescent at the feet
2.seen: At the hem of the pooled gown lies a large ivory crescent, horns turned upward, with the rounded tip of a foot resting inside its curve on the carved lapis floor.

3.name: The glittering sky band
3.seen: Across the upper half, a pale band of glittering mineral runs diagonally from the top left down towards the treetops, set in dark lapis among scattered pinpoints and tiny carved stars of gold.

3.name: Twelve stars and a crown
3.seen: Around the bowed head, twelve small five-pointed ivory stars stand in a ring against the lapis, framing a pointed ivory crown worn over long, wavy hair that falls past the shoulder.

3.name: The moonlit wood
3.seen: Behind the figure a wood rises along the horizon: tall, narrow conifers on the left and in the centre, rounder broadleaf trees to the right, all carved in shades of blue within the lapis.

3.name: The waterfall and stream
3.seen: At the right, a small waterfall spills between carved lapis rocks into a stream that runs forward across the middle ground, passing just beyond the tip of the outstretched rod.

3.name: The star-tipped rod
3.seen: The outstretched arm rests along the scrolled arm of the couch, its fingers loosely holding a slender ivory rod that ends in a small five-pointed star, angled down towards the water.

3.name: Pomegranates on the gown
3.seen: The loose ivory gown pools over the knees and down to one foot on the paving; across its folds are scattered small raised pomegranates, each with a crowned top and a surface dotted with seeds.

3.name: The cushioned couch
3.seen: The Empress reclines on an ivory couch with deep cushions, a scrolled arm at each end, a lattice-carved base and a turned leg, set on a low platform of lapis paving stones.

3.name: The heart with Venus’s sign
3.seen: Leaning against the side of the couch is a heart-shaped shield of paler grey-blue lapis with a raised rim, bearing the circle-and-cross sign of Venus inlaid in gold.

3.name: The field of wheat
3.seen: The whole lower third is filled with tall, ripe wheat carved in blue-grey relief, heavy ears bending in different directions, rising around the couch leg and the edge of the paving.

4.name: The river of stars
4.seen: A diagonal band of glittering silver-grey speckle crosses the lapis sky from the upper right towards the left, among scattered gold pyrite flecks, and fades out above the mountains on the left.

4.name: The bare lapis peaks
4.seen: Jagged mountains carved in paler grey-blue lapis rise behind the throne on both sides, their ridges sharply faceted; the tallest peak rises above the throne back, just to the right of the crown. Nothing grows on them, and no water runs below.

4.name: The ivory crown
4.seen: An ivory crown of upright points, the tallest at the top centre ending in a small ball, sits level on the Emperor’s head. Long wavy hair falls from beneath it to the shoulders.

4.name: The frontal bearded face
4.seen: The Emperor looks straight out at the viewer, brows level, mouth closed behind a full beard that falls in carved waves to the collar. The head is held upright, neither tilted nor turned.

4.name: The gold ankh sceptre
4.seen: The Emperor’s right hand, on the viewer’s left, grips a long ivory staff headed by a gold ankh with a looped top and flared crossbar. Apart from the star flecks, it is the carving’s only gold.

4.name: Four carved ram heads
4.seen: Four curled-horned ram heads are carved in grey-blue lapis on the throne: one at each top corner of the high back and one at the front of each armrest, all turned outward.

4.name: The draped mantle
4.seen: A heavy ivory mantle falls from the shoulders and crosses the chest in one broad diagonal fold, over a tunic with a patterned collar, sleeve and belt; below, its folds cover the knees and fall almost to the boots.

4.name: The orb with its cross
4.seen: In the left hand, on the viewer’s right, the Emperor cradles a small ivory orb from beneath, fingers curled up around its side, a plain cross standing on its top.

4.name: The block-built lapis throne
4.seen: The throne is carved from paler, veined lapis as a set of square blocks: a tall panelled back, armrest pillars with blind arched niches and a carved frieze, all standing on a broad, stepped base.

5.name: The three-tiered crown
5.seen: A tall ivory tiara rises in three stacked tiers, each rimmed with a row of small raised points, and ends in a round knob. A soft cloth falls from beneath it on both sides, framing a calm, level face.

5.name: The hand raised in blessing
5.seen: The figure’s right hand, on your left, lifts to shoulder height, palm turned outward, index and middle fingers raised straight while the others fold down. The sleeve falls back from the wrist in heavy ivory folds.

5.name: The triple-cross staff
5.seen: The other hand, on your right, grips a slender ivory staff at waist height. At its head, three crossbars grow longer as they descend, capped by a small knob, with a rounded knop on the shaft below.

5.name: The layered vestments
5.seen: A full ivory robe falls to the feet beneath a cape draped in deep folds over both arms. A V-shaped collar opens at the throat, and a narrow band runs straight down the chest to the lap.

5.name: Two lapis pillars
5.seen: Two blue columns stand at either side, carved in the lapis itself, with scrolled capitals and stepped bases. The left shaft catches more light than the right. No throne back is carved between them.

5.name: The kneeler with roses
5.seen: At the lower left a figure kneels with back turned, carved in pale blue lapis. Two roses with leaves are incised in fine light lines across the robe’s back; the soles of both feet show beneath the hem.

5.name: The kneeler with a lily
5.seen: At the lower right a second pale blue figure kneels, back to you, facing the seated teacher. A single open lily on a long stem with slender leaves is incised in fine lines on the robe.

5.name: The crossed gold keys
5.seen: Just below the low ledge where the seated figure’s feet rest, two keys cross in an X, toothed bits pointing up and outward, round bows at the bottom. Apart from the pyrite flecks, they are the only gold on the card.

6.name: The gold sun, eyes closed
6.seen: At the top centre, set clear above the angel’s head, a gold sun spreads straight, pointed rays against the lapis night. Its round face is calm, with the eyes closed.

6.name: The angel above the clouds
6.seen: A large winged figure carved in grey-blue lapis, not ivory, rises from a bank of lapis clouds. The wings spread across most of the card’s width; the arms open wide with both hands held open.

6.name: The tree of gold flames
6.seen: Behind the right-hand figure a slender blue tree carries eighteen small gold flames among its carved leaves. Apart from the sun and the scattered gold flecks in the sky, they are the only gold on the card.

6.name: The tree of blue fruit
6.seen: On the left, a leafy tree hangs heavy with round fruit, carved in the same blue lapis as its leaves. None of the fruit is gilded; it stays in shadow against the night.

6.name: The serpent on the trunk
6.seen: A finely scaled serpent in pale grey-blue winds in loose S-bends around the trunk of the fruit tree. Its head rises level with the left-hand figure’s face and points towards it.

6.name: The single blue peak
6.seen: Between the two figures one sharp mountain rises in paler, veined lapis, with low mist lying across its foot. It fills the space between their heads.

6.name: One gaze up, one across
6.seen: The long-haired figure on the left tips the face back to look up at the angel. The curly-haired figure on the right looks level and straight across at the left-hand figure.

6.name: The draped ivory robes
6.seen: Both ivory figures wear classical drapery: on the left a long gown tied at the waist, on the right a short tunic knotted at the hip with a mantle over one shoulder.

6.name: Hands that almost meet
6.seen: Low in the centre, the left figure’s nearer hand is lowered and turned open towards the other. The right figure’s nearer hand hangs loose, fingers curled. A band of dark lapis still separates them.

7.name: The starry arch
7.seen: Above the charioteer, rows of small pale stars carved in the lapis fan out in an arc over rounded arches. The arches spring from four carved lapis columns, two on each side of the chariot.

7.name: The gold star on the crown
7.seen: A small eight-pointed gold star rises from a finial at the centre of the ivory crown. It stands against the lapis just beneath the starry arch, directly above the calm, forward-facing face.

7.name: Gold crescents on the shoulders
7.seen: Each rounded shoulder plate of the ivory armour bears a gold crescent moon, both opening upward. Beneath them the breastplate is worked with fine carved ornament and a belt.

7.name: The staff without reins
7.seen: The charioteer’s hand on the viewer’s left, bent at the elbow, grips a long plain staff with a small rounded knob at the top. The other hand hangs relaxed and empty. No reins appear anywhere.

7.name: The walled city behind
7.seen: Behind the columns, domed buildings, towers and walls are carved in paler lapis on both sides, with hills beyond. On the left a broad road curves out from the city in a long bend towards the chariot.

7.name: The winged gold disc
7.seen: Across the front of the plain, angled ivory chariot body, a gold disc spreads two long feathered wings, with two small shapes hanging beneath it. It is the largest gold element on the card.

7.name: Two spoked wheels
7.seen: Two ivory wheels with raised hubs and straight spokes sit at the lower corners of the veined ivory car, their lower rims just behind the crouching sphinxes. Nothing is harnessed to them or pulling them.

7.name: The ivory sphinx
7.seen: On the left, an ivory sphinx lies with forepaws stretched out and tail curled round its haunch, a small wing carved on its shoulder and a wreath in its hair. Its face turns outward, left.

7.name: The lapis sphinx
7.seen: Its twin on the right is carved from blue lapis in the same crouching pose, almost a mirror image, with a leafy band in its hair and its face turned outward to the right, away from the other.

8.name: The band of the Milky Way
8.seen: A pale, glittering band of white and gold flecks crosses the upper sky on a diagonal, from near the top edge down towards the left border, passing above and to the left of the gold lemniscate.

8.name: The gold lemniscate
8.seen: A figure-eight lying on its side, inlaid in textured gold, floats in the upper centre of the night sky, well above the figure’s bowed head and brighter than any star around it.

8.name: The thin crescent moon
8.seen: On the left, level with the top of the figure’s head, a slender crescent is carved in pale silvery blue, its outer curve facing left, with small gold star flecks scattered to its right and below it.

8.name: The bowed ivory head
8.seen: The figure’s ivory head tilts steeply down towards the lion, eyelids lowered, lips closed. The hair is gathered into a soft knot at the back, with no wreath or ornament.

8.name: Two cypresses on the hill
8.seen: On the far left, two tall, narrow cypress trees stand side by side on a low slope, carved in lighter lapis, with rounded trees beside them and hills rolling away behind.

8.name: Hands on head and jaw
8.seen: One ivory hand rests flat on the crown of the lion’s mane. The other slips its relaxed, slightly curled fingers between the lion’s open jaws, without any visible strain in the wrist or arm.

8.name: The chain of roses
8.seen: From the figure’s waist, a chain of small carved ivory roses and buds crosses the gown diagonally towards the hip and thigh, then slips off the drapery and trails loose to the right, ending in a bud.

8.name: The lapis lion
8.seen: The lion is carved in greyish-blue lapis, not ivory, with a deep wavy mane. Its forepaws are planted, its open-mouthed head lifted to the figure, and its tail sweeps out to the right, curling up at the tip.

8.name: Three fallen roses
8.seen: On the flowering ground between the lion’s forepaws and the figure’s bare feet lies a short ivory sprig bearing three roses and a few small leaves, as if dropped from the garland.

9.name: The band of the Milky Way
9.seen: A pale haze of tiny white specks runs diagonally across the upper sky from lower left to upper right, finer and whiter than the scattered gold flecks of pyrite around it.

9.name: The star cut into the summit
9.seen: Near the top of the highest peak, an eight-pointed star is incised into the pale blue lapis as thin engraved lines. It is not gilded, and it sits above and slightly left of the hooded head.

9.name: The pale mountain range
9.seen: Behind the figure, two main peaks and their ridges are carved in lighter, greyer lapis, streaked like snow and wind-scoured stone, above a long sloping shelf that breaks off sharply at the left.

9.name: The lowered, hooded head
9.seen: The ivory figure is shown in profile facing left, hood drawn well forward, a long wavy beard falling onto the chest. The eyes are cast downward past the outstretched hand, not up at the stars.

9.name: The lantern with its gold star
9.seen: Held out at about chest height, an ivory lantern with a peaked roof and panelled sides hangs from a ring in the fingers. Inside is a small gold eight-pointed star, the only carved element picked out in gold.

9.name: The star on the cliff
9.seen: On the dark face of the left-hand cliff, level with the lantern and to its left, a second eight-pointed star is incised in pale lines into the lapis, small and ungilded.

9.name: The plain ivory staff
9.seen: The second hand grips a long, smooth ivory staff just to the right of the lantern. It runs straight down in front of the robe, and its tip rests near the front lip of the pale ledge.

9.name: The heavy ivory robe
9.seen: A long hooded robe falls in deep vertical folds from shoulders to ankles, the sleeves wide, the hem pooling on the ledge. Only the hands, the face and the toes of one foot show.

9.name: The ledge above the drop
9.seen: The figure stands on a pale, almost white shelf of stone that juts out over a sheer cliff of dark lapis. Below it the rock falls away into the gold-flecked night at the foot of the card.

10.name: The reading angel
10.seen: In the upper left corner a winged figure is seated on a cloud, head bowed over an open book held in both hands. It is carved in the grey-blue of the lapis itself, not in ivory.

10.name: The eagle with its book
10.seen: In the upper right an eagle spreads both wings on a low cloud, talons planted, head turned to the left. An open book stands propped at its side, carved in paler blue stone.

10.name: The river of stars
10.seen: A diagonal band of pale blue and white glitter with gold flecks runs from the top centre down towards the left edge, passing above and left of the sphinx, far denser than the scattered gold flecks elsewhere in the night.

10.name: The sphinx and sword
10.seen: An ivory sphinx with a striped headdress and a raised feathered wing lies along the top of the wheel, forepaws on the rim, a cross-hilted sword laid across its forelegs, point to the right.

10.name: The bare gold wheel
10.seen: A large gold wheel fills the centre: a heavy outer rim around a band of paler lapis, an inner ring over a darker field, and a small ringed hub with a raised boss, joined by eight gold spokes.

10.name: The jackal-headed guardian
10.seen: To the right an ivory figure with a jackal’s head, striped headdress and pleated kilt stands on a small lapis ledge facing the wheel, gripping a tall knob-topped staff and holding a short rod low.

10.name: The descending serpent
10.seen: An ivory serpent loops over the left side of the rim and slides downward, head low at the lower left with a forked tongue showing, tail curling away beneath the wheel.

10.name: The winged bull
10.seen: In the lower left corner a winged bull with curved horns lies on a cloud, head turned towards an open book set beside its forelegs. Like the other corner creatures, it is carved in lapis.

10.name: The winged lion
10.seen: In the lower right corner a winged lion with a thick mane lies on a cloud, one forepaw resting on the top of an open book, tail curled up behind its body.

11.name: The slanting star drift
11.seen: Above the pillars, a band of fine silvery-white flecks crosses the dark lapis sky on a diagonal, from just over the veil towards the upper right; a fainter drift crosses the left margin. Gold star points scatter around.

11.name: The swagged lapis veil
11.seen: A plain cloth carved in lighter, greyish lapis is slung between the tops of the two pillars, sagging in a shallow curve and falling in soft vertical folds behind the figure’s crown and shoulders.

11.name: The pointed ivory crown
11.seen: The figure wears an ivory crown whose tall central point is flanked by smaller points, the outer two flaring outwards; a row of small carved marks runs along the band above long, wavy hair.

11.name: The upright ivory sword
11.seen: Raised in the figure’s right hand, at the viewer’s left, a straight double-edged blade points upwards, its tip rising just above the crown. The fist closes just below a straight crossguard; a round pommel shows beneath it.

11.name: Two fluted pillars
11.seen: Left and right of the throne stand two tall pillars carved in the lighter lapis, with vertical grooves, moulded capitals and stepped bases; the veil hangs from just beneath their capitals.

11.name: The gold-pan scales
11.seen: The figure’s left hand, at the viewer’s right, pinches the ivory handle of a balance. From the knobbed ivory beam, three gold chains hang to each gold pan, and both pans sit at the same height.

11.name: The pale stone throne
11.seen: The figure sits on a low, square-cut throne of pale, whitish-blue stone with a moulded top edge and plain block sides, lighter than the pillars; the ivory robe spills over its front in heavy folds.

11.name: One foot on the step
11.seen: From beneath the hem of the ivory robe a single foot slips forward onto the top step, just left of centre from the viewer’s side; to its right, only the rounded toe of the other foot peeps from the folds.

11.name: Three broad lapis steps
11.seen: Below the throne, three wide steps of lighter, faintly veined lapis descend towards the viewer, each broader than the one above, onto a flat stone floor that fills the base of the card.

12.name: Two pruned living trees
12.seen: Two lapis trunks rise on either side of the figure, their side branches sawn back to round stubs. At the top each trunk forks into a Y that holds the beam, one arm ending in a ringed, cut stump.

12.name: Leaves on sawn wood
12.seen: Small sprigs of pale grey-blue leaves grow from the top of the beam above each trunk and from the sides of both trees, carved lighter than the dark lapis around them.

12.name: The single cord
12.seen: A thin pale cord is wrapped around the middle of the beam, knotted just below it, and drops straight down to a narrow loop tied around the ankle of the raised leg.

12.name: The river of stars
12.seen: A band of gold flecks enters at the top edge, slants down to the left towards the bent knee, and reappears below the halo, trailing away towards the lower right.

12.name: Legs in a figure four
12.seen: The tied leg stays straight. The other bends at the knee, which points to the left, and its shin passes behind the straight leg so that the bare foot emerges on the right.

12.name: The draped loincloth
12.seen: An ivory cloth wraps the hips in soft, heavy folds, gathered and tucked at the waist. It is the only covering on an otherwise bare ivory body.

12.name: Arms folded behind
12.seen: The elbows bend outward at the sides of the torso and the forearms turn in behind the back. The hands stay out of sight; nothing is held or reached for.

12.name: The gold halo
12.seen: Behind the head, which hangs lowest of all, a gold disc is incised with short radiating rays. The face is calm, eyes lowered and almost closed, hair in close ivory curls.

12.name: Roots reaching inward
12.seen: At the foot of each trunk long roots spread across a pebbled lapis ground. The longest of them snake towards the centre from both sides, almost meeting beneath the figure.

13.name: The rose on the banner
13.seen: A long ivory banner hangs from a crossbar on a staff whose tip rises above it like a cross. In its lower half a single full-blown rose is carved in relief, with four leaves on its stem.

13.name: The hooded skeleton rider
13.seen: An ivory skull looks out from a deep ivory hood whose cloak falls over the horse’s back. Beneath it the body is armoured in grey plate; both ivory hands grip the banner staff, one above the other.

13.name: The pale walking horse
13.seen: A large ivory horse walks towards the left at an even pace, the near foreleg lifted. The bridle is plain, the rein runs in a slack curve from the bit up to the rider’s hands, and the eye is calm.

13.name: The gold half-sun
13.seen: On the far horizon, left of the banner staff, a gold half-disc rests on the line of the hills. Two slim lapis towers stand on the skyline, one near each side of the card.

13.name: The fallen King
13.seen: At lower left a figure carved in grey-blue lapis lies full length, cheek to the earth and eyes open, one hand resting before the face. The pale crown is still on, just below the horse’s lifted hoof.

13.name: The figures at prayer
13.seen: At the right edge, carved in blue lapis, a tall mitred bishop stands with palms pressed together, facing the rider. Below, a long-haired figure kneels with hands clasped at the chest and head bowed.

13.name: The child with a flower
13.seen: Beneath the horse’s belly, between its front and hind legs, a small barefoot child in a short tunic, carved in pale grey-blue, steps forward and holds up a small flower in both hands.

13.name: The river and boat
13.seen: A river winds from the horizon down the left side of the card in pale, rippled lapis. Near the lower bend a small boat carries one seated figure holding an oar.

13.name: The glittering sky band
13.seen: A diagonal band of bright, pale blue and silvery chips runs from the top edge down towards the left, passing to the upper left of the banner among small gold star flecks.

14.name: The stream between two goblets
14.seen: The figure holds a stemmed ivory goblet high on the viewer’s left and tilts it; a smooth ivory stream arcs down into a second goblet held lower, near the waist, in the other hand.

14.name: The gold triangle in a square
14.seen: On the breast of the robe a raised square panel is outlined in ivory, with thin lines running inward from its upper corners. Inside it stands an upward-pointing triangle in gold, the largest area of gold on the card.

14.name: The disc on the brow
14.seen: At the hairline, above the centre of the brow, sits a small round ivory disc inside a raised rim that thickens along its lower left edge, so it reads almost as a crescent cradling a disc. The eyes beneath are lowered.

14.name: The raised ivory wings
14.seen: Two large ivory wings rise behind the shoulders, their upper curves level with the head and their long flight feathers falling to about hip height, carved feather by feather against the blue ground.

14.name: The sun on the peak
14.seen: Above the tallest mountain a round disc of grey-blue lapis with a fine pale rim rests on the summit, its lower edge hidden by the rock, ringed with alternating long and short pointed rays.

14.name: The winding path
14.seen: From the stony bank at the right of the pool a pale, finely textured path winds up the slope and disappears behind the figure. A thinner winding line crosses the slopes on the left, beside the irises.

14.name: The irises at the water’s edge
14.seen: At the left, carved in lighter blue lapis, a clump of irises grows beside the pool: three open blooms on tall stems, several closed buds and long blade-shaped leaves rising from the bank.

14.name: The rippled pool
14.seen: The figure stands in a dark pool, robe falling straight into the water, feet hidden. Rings of ripples spread outward from the hem, and a trailing fold sweeps out to touch the stony bank at the right.

14.name: The band of stars
14.seen: Across the upper left of the night sky a diagonal band of tiny pale and silvery chips runs down from the top edge, among scattered gold star flecks set into the lapis.

15.name: The gold star on the brow
15.seen: A small star inlaid in gold sits in the centre of the Devil’s forehead, between two curved ivory horns and above a frowning brow. It has points straight up and straight down.

15.name: The spread bat wings
15.seen: Two broad ivory wings open across the upper card, one on each side of the horned head. They are bat wings: thin ribbed membrane stretched between long finger bones, with a small hooked claw at the top joint of each.

15.name: The raised open hand
15.seen: The Devil’s right arm is lifted to the viewer’s left, bent at the elbow. The open palm faces outward, fingers held together and thumb apart, in front of the ribbed wing.

15.name: The torch held low
15.seen: The Devil’s left hand grips an ivory torch that slants down and outward to the viewer’s right, past the corner of the block. The flame burns at the lower end and curls upward in long tongues.

15.name: The ring and sagging chains
15.seen: A dark iron ring is fixed to the front of the pale lapis block on which the Devil crouches. Two chains hang from it in sagging curves to grey metal collars around the necks of the pair below.

15.name: The horned, chained pair
15.seen: Two ivory figures stand barefoot in front of the block, one on each side of the ring, each with small horns in the hair. One wears a drape over one shoulder, the other a full robe. Both bow their heads, eyes lowered.

15.name: The flame-tipped tail
15.seen: The figure on the left has a slim ivory tail that curves out behind the thigh and ends in a small, upright tuft of flame, echoing the torch the Devil holds above.

15.name: The grape-cluster tail
15.seen: The figure on the right has a tail that curls out beside the robe and ends in a hanging bunch of ivory grapes, with two small vine leaves at the stem.

15.name: The grotto and its openings
15.seen: The scene is set in a hollow of rough blue lapis. Two dark cave mouths open behind the pair, one each side of the block, and a round ringed disc is carved into the rocky floor.

16.name: The gold lightning bolt
16.seen: A bolt of inlaid gold leaves the underside of the cloud, zigzags down to the right and strikes the crown at the tower’s summit, where a thread of gold runs on into a crack in its band.

16.name: The heavy storm cloud
16.seen: Across the upper left, a large cloud is carved in raised, lighter blue lapis, its rounded billows stacked in layers. The bolt emerges from its lower edge rather than from open sky.

16.name: The crown knocked askew
16.seen: At the summit a pointed crown of grey-blue lapis tips sideways off the battlements where the bolt hits it. Beside it, a cracked, crenellated fragment of the tower’s top breaks away to the right.

16.name: The lapis tower
16.seen: A tall tower of fitted lapis blocks rises on the right, topped with battlements. Its walls are carved stone by stone, and a dark arched opening sits low on its wall, half hidden by rock.

16.name: The scattered tongues of flame
16.seen: Small copper-gold flames, shaped like teardrops with flickering tips, are scattered across the dark sky between the tower and the falling figures, most to the left of the walls, a few to the right.

16.name: Fire in the windows
16.seen: Four arched windows on the tower’s face are lit from within by copper-gold flames, one spilling out over its sill. The lower arched opening, near the rock, stays dark.

16.name: The crowned falling figure
16.seen: On the left, an ivory figure falls head first with long hair streaming and a small gold-tinged crown still on the head. One arm stretches out, the other reaches down; the robe billows above bare feet.

16.name: The bareheaded falling figure
16.seen: Below and to the right, a second ivory figure with short curled hair falls head first, arms flung wide and hands open, legs lifted high. Cloth bands gather at both wrists.

16.name: The jagged crag
16.seen: The tower stands on a steep, faceted crag of paler blue lapis that fills the lower right and runs to the card’s bottom edge, its planes cut sharply and crossed by fine cracks.

17.name: The Milky Way along the crack
17.seen: A faint haze of white specks runs diagonally across the upper left sky, from near the top edge down toward the left pillar, following a fine crack in the lapis and dotted with gold flecks.

17.name: The ibis in the tree
17.seen: At the upper right a leafy tree, carved in pale grey-blue lapis, rises from a small hill. A long-legged bird with a long down-curved beak stands on one branch, facing left toward the stars.

17.name: Seven silver stars
17.seen: Seven small many-rayed stars are cut into the lapis in pale silvery blue, not gilded. They form a symmetrical arch around the gold star: one directly above it, three stepping down on each side.

17.name: The great gold star
17.seen: At the centre of the sky hangs a large eight-pointed star in raised gold, four long rays alternating with four shorter ones, set in a soft haze of gold dust above the bowed head.

17.name: The jug raised high
17.seen: At the left, one ivory arm lifts a jug above shoulder height, the hand gripping its handle, and tips it so a single clear thread of water falls straight down into the pool, raising rings.

17.name: The two lapis pillars
17.seen: Two slender columns of lighter, mottled lapis stand at the left and right edges on the grassy bank, each with a plain capital and base, framing the figure, the pool and the star between them.

17.name: The draped kneeling figure
17.seen: The ivory figure kneels on the bank in a thin, high-belted robe, hair gathered up with loose locks falling. The head bows toward the right-hand jug, eyes lowered, and one bare foot rests in the pool.

17.name: The streams across the bank
17.seen: At the right, a second jug held lower at arm’s length pours a stream that splits as it falls, landing as several thin, wavy rivulets that run across the grassy bank toward the pool.

17.name: The pool and its crescent
17.seen: The dark pool across the foot of the card is carved with rings of ripples where the falling water and the foot touch it. Left of centre, a small crescent moon is cut into its surface.

18.name: The crescent in the disc
18.seen: A large ivory disc fills the upper centre, ringed by alternating straight and wavy rays. Carved in raised relief inside it, a crescent curves around the upper left, its lower horn ending at the brow of a face.

18.name: The sleeping face
18.seen: Within the disc a calm face is carved in profile, turned toward the right, the one visible eye closed, lips together. Just below it, on the lower edge of the disc, sits a single raised teardrop.

18.name: The clouds across the disc
18.seen: Two soft ivory clouds drift at either side of the disc. The left one crosses the lower edge of the disc and its rays; the right one lies over the rays at the lower right.

18.name: Thirteen falling drops
18.seen: Below the disc, thirteen small ivory teardrops hang in loose rows between the lowest rays and the mountain tops, pointed end up, rounded end down, shaped like the single tear carved on the disc.

18.name: The two castles
18.seen: On far hills to left and right stand two small castles carved in grey-blue lapis, each a cluster of towers with pointed roofs and battlements, facing each other across the winding path.

18.name: The gold path
18.seen: A winding road of gold leaf starts in the pool, its gold spilling across the water, climbs between the two animals and the castles, narrows, and disappears into a gap in the mountains.

18.name: The howling wolf
18.seen: On a grassy ledge at the left edge of the water, a shaggy-coated wolf in grey-blue lapis stands with its head thrown back, muzzle raised to the moon, mouth open in a howl.

18.name: The upward-gazing dog
18.seen: Opposite the wolf, on a rocky bank at the right edge of the water, a smooth-coated dog with a drooping ear lifts its face to the moon, mouth only slightly open.

18.name: The crayfish in the pool
18.seen: At the bottom centre, a crayfish carved in grey-blue lapis rests in the dark pool, both claws raised, its long feelers curving up along the gold where the path begins.

19.name: The gilded sun face
19.seen: A large gold disc fills the upper sky, carved with a calm, frontal face whose eyes are closed. Broad straight rays, thin spikes and wavy, flame-like rays alternate all the way around it.

19.name: The band of stars
19.seen: A diagonal band of glittering, silvery chips crosses the lapis sky from beside the sun’s lower left rays down to the right, fading out above the child, among scattered gold star flecks.

19.name: Four lapis sunflowers
19.seen: Above the wall grow sunflowers carved in blue-grey lapis, not gold: two open blooms at the left, and at the right one open bloom beside a smaller head turned in towards the centre.

19.name: The wreath and feather
19.seen: The child’s head is circled by a wreath of small ivory leaves and blossoms, with a single upright feather rising from its front. Beneath it the child’s eyes are closed, like the sun’s.

19.name: The child with open arms
19.seen: An ivory child sits bareback on the horse, a light ivory cloth hanging from the shoulders and gathered across the lap. One arm is flung wide with the palm open; the other hand grips the banner staff.

19.name: The ivory banner
19.seen: From a slender staff topped with a round knob, a long, plain ivory banner streams out to the right of the rider, twisting in loose folds into forked, ribbon-like ends. It carries no emblem.

19.name: The lapis garden wall
19.seen: A low wall of squared lapis blocks, paler and brighter blue than the sky, runs the full width of the card behind the horse, its top edge close to the child’s shoulders.

19.name: The white horse
19.seen: A large ivory horse stands calmly facing left, all four hooves on the grassy ground. It wears a simple bridle but no saddle, and a slack rein runs back to the child’s waist, held by neither hand.

19.name: Two winged cherub heads
19.seen: Level with the horse’s legs, two ivory cherub heads with small feathered wings and draped collars float against the lapis, one in front of the forelegs and one under the belly, between fore and hind legs.

20.name: The trumpeting angel
20.seen: Carved in pale grey-blue lapis rather than ivory, the angel leans out of the clouds with wings spread towards both upper corners, head bowed, eyes lowered, one hand at the mouthpiece and the other lower on the shaft.

20.name: The gold trumpet
20.seen: A long, straight gold trumpet runs from the angel’s lips down through the clouds and ends in a wide flared bell turned straight down towards the three figures, the broadest stretch of gold in the scene.

20.name: The banner with the cross
20.seen: Two fine cords hang from the rim of the bell and hold a short rod with gold ends. From it hangs a small ivory banner with a wavy lower edge, marked with a simple cross outlined in gold.

20.name: The falling trail of light
20.seen: Left of the trumpet, a narrow diagonal stream of silver and gold chips runs from beneath the clouds down towards the mountain peaks on the left, denser and brighter than the scattered star flecks around it.

20.name: The pale mountain range
20.seen: Beyond the sea, a range of pale grey-blue peaks carved in the lapis stretches across the whole horizon, rising highest near each side of the card and dipping low behind the banner.

20.name: The bearded figure stepping out
20.seen: On the left, an ivory figure with curly hair and a full beard looks up towards the angel. Both arms hang open with palms turned upward, and one bare foot steps forward over the coffin’s front rim.

20.name: The child with raised arms
20.seen: At the centre, a curly-haired child in a short ivory tunic stands with back to the viewer, both arms raised high in a wide V, fingers spread, bare feet planted on the floor of the coffin.

20.name: The long-haired figure turning upward
20.seen: On the right, an ivory figure with long wavy hair, seen in profile, lifts the face towards the angel. The arms open low and wide, and the robe falls to one bare foot inside the coffin.

20.name: Open coffins on the sea
20.seen: The sea is scattered with many open, lidless coffins of pale grey-blue lapis, floating out to the horizon. The three nearest are larger and each holds a standing figure; the child’s sits squarely at the centre.

21.name: The floating dancer
21.seen: An ivory figure in sheer, lifting drapery hangs at the centre of the oval, touching nothing. A gold leafy circlet sits in the hair, the head turns to the right, and the legs cross at the knee above bare, downward-pointing feet.

21.name: The bound laurel wreath
21.seen: A tall oval of gold laurel leaves encloses the dancer. At the top and again at the bottom, the two branches meet under a gold ribbon binding whose bands cross in a clear X.

21.name: Two slim gold wands
21.seen: The raised hand on the viewer’s left holds a slim gold wand diagonally, its knobbed upper end tilted towards the head. The lowered hand on the right grips a second wand almost upright, a small round knob at its top.

21.name: The head in the clouds
21.seen: In the top left corner a human head carved in grey-blue lapis emerges from rounded clouds, seen in profile facing right, with long, wind-blown hair and no wings.

21.name: The eagle with lifted wings
21.seen: In the top right corner a large lapis eagle perches on a bank of cloud, both wings lifted and half open, its hooked beak turned left towards the centre of the card.

21.name: The lion on the clouds
21.seen: At lower left a heavily maned lion in grey-blue lapis rests its forepaws on a cloud beside the wreath, head in three-quarter view and turned towards the centre, above a rocky river valley.

21.name: The horned bull
21.seen: At lower right a heavy lapis bull with curved horns and a curly brow rises out of clouds, its head turned towards the centre and its body fading into the card’s edge.

21.name: Two children with wands
21.seen: Below the wreath two small ivory children, each trailing a ribbon of drapery, dance on rocky ledges either side of a winding river, and each holds up a tiny gold wand.

21.name: The glittering sky band
21.seen: On the left a diagonal band of pale, glinting chips runs up from the card’s edge across the lapis, passing behind the laurel and on into the oval towards the dancer’s drapery.

22.name: The gold flame-bud
22.seen: At the top of the staff sits a closed bud of gold, its pointed petals rising together like a single flame, cupped in ivory sepals. It is the only gilded part of the carving.

22.name: The living staff
22.seen: A straight ivory staff, knotted like a cut branch and blunt at its lower end, rises from the hand to the bud; small sprigs of serrated leaves grow from it above and below the fist.

22.name: The hand from the cloud
22.seen: An ivory hand reaches in from the right, its wrist lost in the cloud’s curls. Four fingers wrap the staff with their nails turned towards you, and the thumb presses upward along its right side.

22.name: Spiralling ivory cloud
22.seen: A broad ivory cloud crosses the card from the left edge to the right, its surface carved into tight spirals and scrolls; it billows highest on the right, where the hand emerges.

22.name: Six falling leaves
22.seen: Six loose ivory leaves drift in the lapis around the staff, four above the cloud and two below it, each turned at a different angle as if just shaken free.

22.name: Full moon and Milky Way
22.seen: In the upper right hangs a round ivory full moon with faint craters, while a glittering band of pale mineral and gold flecks crosses the sky from the top edge down towards the left.

22.name: Castle on the hill
22.seen: Far off on the left, a castle of pointed towers and turrets crowns a hill, carved in pale grey-blue lapis in the same low relief as the hills and trees around it.

22.name: The winding river
22.seen: A silver-blue river curls in wide bends from the far hills down to the bottom edge of the card, between wooded slopes and low banks of mist carved in lapis.

22.name: Two ivory cypresses
22.seen: On the right-hand hill stand two slim cypresses carved in ivory, the left one taller, their pointed crowns reaching upward. They are the only trees on the card not carved in lapis.

23.name: The gold-budded wand
23.seen: The taller wand, on the right, is a knotted staff of grey-blue lapis with small side shoots. At its tip a bud opens in gilded leaves, the only gold beyond the scattered stars.

23.name: Two arching laurel branches
23.seen: Two leafy branches carved in pale grey-blue lapis rise on either side of the scene and bend inward over it, their tips drawing close above the figure’s head without joining.

23.name: The level gaze
23.seen: The ivory figure, with curling hair and beard, stands in strict profile facing right. The eyes look level and outward, above the globe, towards the shaft of the held wand, while the bay lies behind the shoulders.

23.name: The small ivory globe
23.seen: At chest height one hand cradles a smooth ivory globe from beneath, fingers curled around its lower curve. Faint incised lines of coastlines and continents run across its surface.

23.name: The wand fixed in rings
23.seen: The left wand, slimmer and shorter, with small knots along its shaft and a closed bud at its tip, rises from the wall. About halfway up it is held by a clasp of two dark, rust-brown rings joined across the shaft.

23.name: The bay and far shore
23.seen: To the left, in lighter blue lapis, a curved bay opens between rocky cliffs, with a cluster of small houses on the far slope and a range of mountains beyond.

23.name: Battlements and round tower
23.seen: The barefoot figure stands on crenellated walls of blue lapis, built in two tiers with a small square turret on the left. On the right they end in a round tower with a corbelled, crenellated top and narrow slit windows.

23.name: The eight-pointed star
23.seen: Carved into the face of the wall just below the figure’s bare feet, a small eight-pointed star in pale grey-blue lapis sits directly above the crossed flowers.

23.name: The crossed rose and lily
23.seen: Below the star, a full-blown rose in grey-blue lapis and an open lily in a paler, almost ivory tone are carved in relief, their leafy stems crossing in an X, with tufts of grass on either side.

24.name: Two gold leaves
24.seen: Near the top of the middle wand, two small gold leaves grow from opposite sides of the lapis branch, the right one slightly lower. Apart from the star flecks, they are the only gold on the card.

24.name: The band of stars
24.seen: A pale, glittering band of mineral crosses the dark lapis sky diagonally from the upper right toward the left, passing behind the left wand, with small gold flecks scattered like stars around it.

24.name: Three planted wands
24.seen: Three wands of grey-blue lapis, knotted with short broken-off side shoots, stand upright with their feet in the rock. The figure fills the wide gap between the left and middle wands; the right wand stands nearer the middle.

24.name: The figure seen from behind
24.seen: An ivory figure with short curled hair stands with its back to the viewer, wrapped in a long, heavy cloak with a hood gathered at the neck; the hem falls to the feet on the rock.

24.name: The hand on the wand
24.seen: The figure’s right arm comes out from under the cloak, and its hand closes around the middle wand a little below shoulder height. It is the only wand the figure touches.

24.name: Three ships under sail
24.seen: On the sea below, three small ships carved in pale lapis sail with canvas set: one further out, between the left wand and the figure, and two nearer the viewer, close to the left and right edges.

24.name: The sea and far shores
24.seen: A wide sea, finely lined with ripples, runs to a straight horizon that crosses behind the figure at about mid-back, with rocky headlands and hills carved in paler lapis on both sides of the card.

24.name: The high rock
24.seen: The figure and all three wands stand on a broad, flat-topped outcrop of faceted lapis that fills the lower quarter of the card, its carved faces dropping steeply toward the sea.

25.name: Four living wands
25.seen: Four slender wands carved in blue lapis relief stand planted in the ground, two on each side of the dancers. Carved vines twist up every shaft, and each tip breaks into sprouting leaves against the night.

25.name: The golden leaf finial
25.seen: High on the far-left wand, just above the knot that ties the garland, sits a three-lobed leaf ornament in gold. Apart from star flecks and a diagonal trail of pyrite in the sky, it is the only gold on the card.

25.name: The fruited garland
25.seen: A heavy garland of leaves and clustered round fruits, carved in lighter blue, is tied to the wands with knotted cords high on the posts and swags low across the middle, in front of the castle.

25.name: The castle behind the canopy
25.seen: Beyond the garland rises a walled castle carved low in greyish-blue lapis: round crenellated towers, some with pointed roofs, and in front, a small gabled house with an arched doorway beside an arched bridge.

25.name: The gathering by the walls
25.seen: Tiny carved figures stand in groups on the ground before the castle walls, beneath the left swag of the garland, with more near the bridge on the right; none is clearly detailed.

25.name: Two sprigs of blossom
25.seen: The dancers lift two small sprigs of ivory blossom and leaves above their heads: one in the left dancer’s outer hand, stretching toward the joined hands, the other raised high in the right dancer’s outer hand.

25.name: Hands meeting overhead
25.seen: Both dancers raise both arms. At the top of the arc their inner hands meet and touch, the dancer on the right reaching across, while each outer hand holds a sprig aloft.

25.name: The leafy circlet
25.seen: The dancer on the left wears a small circlet of leaves over hair gathered up at the back; the dancer on the right has short, dense curls and no wreath. The two faces turn toward each other, smiling.

25.name: Two barefoot dancers
25.seen: Two ivory figures dance barefoot on rough lapis ground in the foreground, one in a long flowing gown, one in a short tunic tied with a sash, light drapes and hems lifting with the movement.

26.name: The Milky Way band
26.seen: A glittering drift of silvery flecks crosses the upper sky diagonally, from lower left to upper right, with small gold star flecks scattered on either side in the dark lapis.

26.name: The gold flame
26.seen: At the tip of the tallest staff, higher than every other, a small flame worked in gold burns upward against the night. Apart from the star flecks, it is the only gold on the card.

26.name: The pale crescent
26.seen: Low in the sky on the left, a thin crescent moon carved in paler lapis opens to the right, resting just above a bank of rounded clouds on the horizon.

26.name: The crossing staves
26.seen: Long, smooth ivory staves cross and recross above the heads, pointing every way at once. At least seven separate upper tips can be counted against the sky, more than the five of the title.

26.name: The upturned face
26.seen: At the right, the rearmost figure stretches one arm high to grip a staff near where several cross, and lifts the face upward and to the left, toward the crossing staves rather than toward any other figure.

26.name: Five young figures
26.seen: Five barefoot, curly-haired youths in short belted ivory tunics lunge and lean inward from both sides, arms raised, shoulders overlapping. Their faces are calm and intent rather than angry.

26.name: The low hills
26.seen: Behind the group, low peaks and ridges carved in greyer lapis run along the horizon at both the left and right edges, beneath rounded banks of lighter blue cloud.

26.name: Bare feet, open ground
26.seen: Every visible foot is bare. Legs brace in wide lunges, one leg bent and one stretched behind, on rough, scored lapis ground that shows no path, grass or marked boundary.

27.name: The wreath on the staff
27.seen: At the top of the rider’s staff an open ring of pale, silvery laurel leaves rises against the night. A small sprig of gold leaves is tied where the ring meets the staff, on its left.

27.name: The laurel crown
27.seen: A carved ivory crown of laurel leaves sits on the rider’s curled hair. The rider’s head is in profile, facing right and level, looking ahead rather than down at the crowd.

27.name: Wands raised by the crowd
27.seen: Four staves rise among the walkers: two knotted staves slant back from the raised hands of the two rearmost walkers, one stands upright in a bearded walker’s fist, and a shorter one lifts behind it.

27.name: The walking companions
27.seen: Five walkers follow on foot, stepping towards the right. Two are carved in ivory; the helmeted, capped and bare-headed figures set back are in grey-blue lapis. Faces turn up towards the rider; one raises an empty hand.

27.name: The white horse
27.seen: An ivory horse, larger than any walker, carries the rider to the right. Its neck arches, a bridle and reins run to the rider’s lowered hand, and the front leg at the far right is lifted high.

27.name: The rider’s bare foot
27.seen: Below the tasselled saddle-cloth, with its embroidered border and roundel, the rider’s leg hangs relaxed and the foot is bare, toes pointing down towards the road, with no stirrup or boot.

27.name: Temples on the skyline
27.seen: Carved in paler lapis behind the procession: on the left, low hills and a small pedimented temple between two columns; on the right, a larger colonnade with a broken roofline at the card’s edge.

27.name: The cracked road
27.seen: Every foot and hoof rests on one narrow road of pale, greyish lapis, crazed with cracks like old paving. Below it the deep blue stone continues to the card’s bottom edge, flecked with gold.

27.name: The glittering vein
27.seen: A long band of glittering pale mineral crosses the sky diagonally from upper right to lower left, above the procession, among scattered gold flecks shaped like tiny stars.

28.name: The turned head
28.seen: The ivory figure’s head, crowned with short, tousled curls, turns in sharp profile toward the right edge of the card, jaw set, while chest and hips still face you.

28.name: Gold flame on the staff
28.seen: At the staff’s left-hand end, just beyond the left fist, a small crown of gold flame curls upward in several tongues. It is the only gold on the figure or the rock.

28.name: The staff held crosswise
28.seen: One long, smooth ivory staff is gripped overhand in both fists and held level across the chest, its plain far end reaching well past the shoulder on the right.

28.name: Six wands of grey lapis
28.seen: Six rough wands, three on each side, rise from behind the crag near the figure’s feet and fan outward. Carved in grey-blue lapis with knotted, twig-stubbed tips, all six lean away from the figure.

28.name: A shoe and a boot
28.seen: The legs are planted wide with knees bent and weight low. The foot on the left wears a soft, low slipper; the foot on the right wears a calf boot beneath a rolled cuff of cloth.

28.name: The cracked crag
28.seen: The figure stands on the uneven top of a crag carved in mid-blue lapis with pale, worn edges, faceted and split by dark fissures, falling away steeply below; lower ridges show behind it on the left.

28.name: Wind-driven clouds
28.seen: Behind the head and shoulders, clouds carved in lighter blue lapis curl and stream sideways, and fine wind lines run horizontally behind the figure’s arms and torso on both sides.

28.name: Glittering vein across the sky
28.seen: A long diagonal vein of glittering pale mineral crosses the dark lapis from the top edge down toward the left edge, passing just left of the clouds; small gold flecks are scattered across the whole sky.

29.name: Eight wands in parallel flight
29.seen: Eight ivory wands, each with a rounded bud-like head and a slimmer knobbed foot, slant together across the lapis sky from upper right to lower left, closely spaced and parallel, none crossing another.

29.name: Leaves behind the heads
29.seen: Just behind the rounded heads of several wands, short twigs put out small clusters of almond-shaped ivory leaves, carved with fine central veins; other wands carry only small bare nubs, or nothing at all.

29.name: The band of starlight
29.seen: A diagonal band of glittering pale mineral crosses the upper left of the dark lapis, slanting down to the left like the wands, while small gold flecks are scattered like stars across the whole sky.

29.name: The shorter bare wand
29.seen: One wand is shorter than the rest: its rounded head stops near the centre of the card, well to the left of the other heads, and its whole shaft carries no leaves.

29.name: Three gold leaves
29.seen: At the lower-left end of the longest wand, three leaves of gold spread outward like an arrowhead, hovering just above the ridge of the hills. They are the only carved gold on the card.

29.name: The cottage on the hillside
29.seen: Carved in pale grey-blue lapis on a slope right of centre, a gabled cottage with a chimney and a many-paned window sits among rounded trees, below a higher peak.

29.name: Bridge and small waterfall
29.seen: Below and left of the cottage, a stream passes a small arched bridge and spills over a low fall into a wider pool, all carved in the lighter blue of the landscape.

29.name: The river in the foreground
29.seen: A broad stretch of water fills the lower centre, its surface scored with fine horizontal lines, held between smooth rounded banks, with a dark foreground slope in front of it.

30.name: The Milky Way band
30.seen: A pale diagonal drift of silvery flecks crosses the dark lapis sky from lower left to upper right, high above the figure, with small gold stars scattered on either side of it.

30.name: The gold sprig
30.seen: At the tip of the figure’s own staff, just above the bandaged head, a small sprig of gold leaves opens upward, gleaming against the dark lapis night.

30.name: The bandaged head
30.seen: A cloth bandage is wound around the figure’s head and tied in a knot at the back, two loose ends trailing to the left. The bearded face is seen in profile, turned to the right, eyes open and watchful.

30.name: Both hands on the staff
30.seen: Two ivory hands grip the staff one above the other, drawn close to the chest, the upper fist just below the bearded chin. The shoulders round forward over them.

30.name: Twelve blue staves
30.seen: Twelve knotted staves carved in the blue lapis itself, each with cut branch stubs, stand upright on the rim of the oval ground, six on either side of the figure, some nearer to us and some behind.

30.name: The hills beyond
30.seen: Beyond the ring, rolling hills and a low mountain ridge are carved in greyer lapis, with small bushes and rocks, running to the horizon on both sides behind the staves.

30.name: The planted ivory staff
30.seen: One pale ivory staff, unlike the blue ones, runs from the gold sprig past the figure’s tunic to the ground, its foot planted just beside the forward foot, with the figure leaning into it.

30.name: The trodden oval
30.seen: The staves stand along the rim of an oval of ground set off from the lapis around it. Its surface is scored with curving, swirling lines, and the figure’s feet and staff rest inside it.

31.name: The fanned ivory wands
31.seen: Long ivory staves rise from the figure’s grip and fan out above and beyond the bowed head against the night sky. Eight rough tips are clearly visible, each shaft knotted with small cut-off twig stubs.

31.name: The gold sprig
31.seen: A small sprig of gold leaves on a thin gold stem sprouts from among the upright wands, high above the figure’s head. It is the only gold on the carved figure and its load.

31.name: The bowed, wrapped head
31.seen: The head is wrapped in ivory cloth knotted at the crown and pulled low over the brow, so no eye shows; curls escape around the ear. Only nose, lips and chin appear, turned towards the ground.

31.name: Two clutching hands
31.seen: One hand grips the bundle just below the chin; the other, a closed fist on a bent arm, holds it lower against the chest. Below the grip, the lower ends of the staves splay out towards the viewer’s left.

31.name: The walled town ahead
31.seen: On the right, carved in lighter blue lapis, a walled town rises among trees: an arched gateway, a tall tower with a pointed roof, clustered rooftops and low hills behind.

31.name: The winding road
31.seen: A pale road winds up from the flat ground ahead of the figure’s front foot, curving between furrowed fields and trees until it reaches the arched gate of the town.

31.name: The labouring stride
31.seen: Bare, muscular legs step towards the right in soft boots slouched at the ankles. The back heel lifts off the ground, both knees bend, and the whole body leans far forward from the hips.

31.name: The house left behind
31.seen: Behind the figure on the left, a small farmhouse with a single chimney sits among bushes on a rise above ploughed fields, carved in the same muted blue lapis as the landscape.

31.name: Glittering vein and stars
31.seen: A pale, glittering mineral vein crosses the dark lapis sky diagonally from the top edge down towards the left side, while small gold flecks are scattered across the sky like stars.

32.name: The gold flame-bud
32.seen: At the tip of the staff, two upward-curving ivory sepals cup a pointed shape of gold, half bud and half flame; it is the brightest point on the card.

32.name: The upturned face
32.seen: The ivory figure is carved in profile, head tipped back and chin lifted, eyes raised toward the gold tip of the staff and the sky beyond it.

32.name: The feather in the cap
32.seen: A single carved feather rises from a small ornament on the band of a rounded ivory cap and sweeps back toward the right, above a cluster of tight curls at the nape.

32.name: The glittering sky band
32.seen: A diagonal band of silvery-blue crystalline sparkle crosses the upper lapis sky from the upper left down toward the right, scattered with tiny gold star flecks around it.

32.name: Gold star flecks
32.seen: Small points of gold are scattered across the dark lapis sky, most of them round flecks, a few with tiny pointed rays that catch the light like miniature stars.

32.name: The tall ivory staff
32.seen: A straight, slender ivory staff, taller than the figure, rests its foot on the ground just left of the feet; the raised hand grips it at about head height, the other lower down, above the belt.

32.name: The tunic of salamanders
32.seen: The short ivory tunic, with a V-neck border, banded cuffs, a round-buckled belt and a sash knotted at the hip, is scattered with small curling lizard-like creatures incised in pale gold-brown.

32.name: Two carved pyramids
32.seen: On the right horizon two pyramids are cut in greyish lapis, one larger in front and a smaller one set behind it to the right, their faces lightly lined.

32.name: The blue dune ground
32.seen: Low rolling dunes are carved across the lower card in paler, textured blue lapis, their crests running in soft horizontal ridges behind and beneath the standing figure.

33.name: The gold flame
33.seen: At the far end of the wand a gold flame rises in several curling tongues, bending slightly back as if in a headwind; with the scattered star flecks, it is the only gold on the card.

33.name: Plumed helmet, streaming back
33.seen: The rider wears a close ivory helmet with a pointed crown and a small peak over curly hair; a long plume springs from the top and streams back towards the left in loose strands.

33.name: The bare wand, held forward
33.seen: A long, smooth ivory wand is held out at the full stretch of one arm, angled upward over the horse’s head; it has no leaves or knots, only the flame at its tip.

33.name: Two pyramids behind
33.seen: Two pyramids of paler, greyer lapis stand on the far left horizon, a larger one and a smaller one just to its right, with low ridges beyond and a flat, rippled plain stretching behind the horse.

33.name: The horse’s bowed head
33.seen: The ivory horse’s head is tucked down and in, ears pricked forward, eye calm; a carved bridle crosses the face and the reins run back to the rider’s other fist, held low near the belt.

33.name: Carved tunic motifs
33.seen: The rider’s belted ivory tunic falls over the saddle in soft folds, carved with small low-relief motifs: curling forms with trailing tails, scattered across the chest and skirt.

33.name: Forelegs in mid-leap
33.seen: Both forelegs are lifted clear of the ground and folded at the knee, hooves hanging; the hind legs stretch back and down, hooves planted beside tufts of dry scrub.

33.name: The spurred heel
33.seen: Below a carved knee plate, the rider’s armoured shin ends in a pointed shoe with a strap across the instep; a small spur projects from the heel, below the horse’s belly and touching nothing.

34.name: The wand with gold leaves
34.seen: On the viewer’s left, the Queen’s right hand grips an ivory wand whose foot rests on the dais; small budding stubs knot the shaft, which ends in three gilded leaves, the only gilded carving on the card.

34.name: The sunflower in hand
34.seen: In the Queen’s left hand, on the viewer’s right, a single ivory sunflower rises on a slender stalk with two broad leaves, its open face turned toward the viewer.

34.name: The pale seated cat
34.seen: An ivory cat sits upright at the front of the dais beside the Queen’s visible foot, eyes open and facing the viewer, its tail curled forward along the step.

34.name: Crown and temple spirals
34.seen: An open ivory crown of tall points with a leaf-shaped central spike and a round boss on its band; a small carved spiral sits at each side of the head, just above the long hair.

34.name: Four lions of the throne
34.seen: Two lions rear on their hind legs inside the arch, facing each other across a carved sun; two more sit upright on the tops of the square pillars, all cut in lighter blue lapis.

34.name: The carved sun in the arch
34.seen: At the peak of the rounded arch a many-rayed sun is carved in lapis, its pointed rays spreading like petals, set between the two rearing lions and directly above the crown.

34.name: Full moon and two crescents
34.seen: Above the leafy crest of the throne, a full moon in pale grey-blue lapis hangs at upper left with a thin crescent beside it; a second crescent sits at upper right among small bright flecks.

34.name: Sea, boat and trees
34.seen: Behind the Queen, carved in pale lapis, calm water carries a small sailing boat on the left, with a leafy tree on each shore and low mountains rising beyond.

34.name: Leaves carved into the throne
34.seen: Leafy sprigs are carved in relief on the tall panels at the base of both throne pillars, and a row of broad leaves runs along the top of the arch, all in blue lapis.

35.name: Lion heads on the throne
35.seen: Two lion heads carved in greyed lapis sit on the top corners of the throne back, manes thick, facing away from each other, joined by a scrolling crest that rises to a central palmette.

35.name: Salamanders on the frieze
35.seen: Below the crest, a carved band on the throne shows two lapis salamanders with curling tails and open mouths, one on each side of a round many-petalled rosette, both leaning in towards it.

35.name: Bird in the carved panel
35.seen: Behind the King’s head, the throne back is a lapis panel carved with leafy branches and a large open flower; a small bird perches on a slender stem near the top, facing left.

35.name: The gold flame
35.seen: At the top of the staff, above a small ivory cup of petals, a flame of polished gold rises in several tongues; it is the only gold on the figure and the throne.

35.name: Crown of trefoil points
35.seen: An ivory crown with five raised points, each tipped with a carved trefoil and the tallest at the centre, sits over long wavy hair; the bearded face is turned in profile to the right.

35.name: The flowering staff
35.seen: A tall ivory branch knotted with short side twigs rises from the front corner of the dais to above the King’s head; one hand grips it at arm’s length, and a small blossom and bud open near the top.

35.name: Full moon over the valley
35.seen: At the far left a full moon, carved as a pale lapis disc, hangs above low hills; a small flock of birds flies beside it and a river winds through the valley below.

35.name: Salamander-patterned robe
35.seen: The ivory cloak and gown are incised with small creatures, most long-bodied and long-tailed like salamanders; the hems carry a patterned border and a round clasp fastens the cloak at the chest.

35.name: The salamander on the dais
35.seen: A small speckled salamander carved in grey-blue lapis crawls across the top of the dais, its tail curled round the foot of the staff and its head raised towards the King’s ivory shoes.

36.name: The ivory cloud and column
36.seen: A billowing ivory cloud spreads across the upper sky, its edges drawn out into wisps on both sides; from its centre a smooth, rounded ivory column descends and ends at the dove’s tail.

36.name: The dove with the wafer
36.seen: An ivory dove dives head first beneath the column, wings spread wide, holding a small round wafer in its beak just above the cup; a thin glassy stream runs from beneath the wafer into the bowl.

36.name: The gold star on the bowl
36.seen: Set on the front of the ivory bowl is a gold star with eight slender points, the only gold among the ivory carvings; beneath it runs a band of carved leaves.

36.name: The ivory chalice
36.seen: A wide, deep ivory chalice with a moulded rim, a carved knop on its stem and a broad lobed foot decorated in low relief, held upright at the centre of the card.

36.name: The hand from the left
36.seen: An ivory forearm enters from the left, its far end fading softly into the lapis; the hand closes firmly around the stem just below the knop, and two streams of water run across the arm.

36.name: Five streams to the pool
36.seen: Four glassy streams rise from inside the bowl and arch over the rim, two to each side; a fifth drops straight down the centre below the foot. All five reach the pool, with drops falling between them.

36.name: Lotuses on the pool
36.seen: Pale carved lotus blossoms and flat round pads float on a rippled blue pool; rings spread where the streams strike the water, and banks of grey-blue cloud frame the pool at both lower corners.

36.name: Blue peaks on either side
36.seen: Jagged peaks carved in lighter blue lapis rise on both sides of the cup at mid-height, with a stand of small carved trees on the right-hand shore below them.

36.name: The glittering diagonal trail
36.seen: Below the cloud’s left wing a trail of faceted, glittering crystals runs diagonally down to the left edge of the card, among small gold star flecks scattered across the dark lapis sky.

37.name: Milky Way over the meeting
37.seen: A glittering band of pale mineral runs diagonally across the upper card from lower left to upper right, among small gold star flecks scattered over the dark ultramarine sky.

37.name: The winged lion’s head
37.seen: At the top of the central staff a lion’s head with open jaws and a full mane spreads two broad feathered wings, carved in the same pale greyish blue lapis as the distant hills.

37.name: Twin serpents on the staff
37.seen: Two serpents wind around each other and around a straight staff beneath the lion, then raise their heads at the same height to face each other just under the wings.

37.name: Laurel on the left
37.seen: The left-hand figure wears a close wreath of pointed laurel leaves over short curls, and a round clasp fastens the ivory cloak at the shoulder. The head is bowed, eyes lowered toward the hands.

37.name: Flowering wreath on the right
37.seen: The right-hand figure wears a wreath of leaves opening into small flowers, with long wavy hair falling past the shoulders. This figure looks straight across, level, toward the other’s face.

37.name: The cottage between them
37.seen: Far behind the couple, carved into the blue lapis hills, stands a small single-storey house with a chimney, a door and small windows, framed by rounded trees. The caduceus staff rises from behind its roof.

37.name: The plain raised cup
37.seen: The left-hand figure lifts a plain, unadorned ivory cup in front of the chest, fingers wrapped around its stem just beneath the bowl, held upright above the other, reaching hand.

37.name: Hands almost meeting
37.seen: At the centre of the lower card the two free hands reach toward each other: one extended with fingers pointing forward, the other open with the palm showing. A thin band of lapis still separates the fingertips.

37.name: The gold heart on the cup
37.seen: The right-hand figure holds a stemmed goblet low at the waist, fingers curled beneath the bowl. Set into the ivory bowl is a heart of glittering gold, the only gold on the card besides the star flecks.

38.name: The gold heart
38.seen: A small heart of inlaid gold sits on the bowl of the central cup; apart from the star flecks in the dark border, it is the only gold on the card and the brightest point at its centre.

38.name: Three raised cups
38.seen: Three ivory goblets on short knopped stems meet above the heads of the dancers, each held up by a single hand; the central one is larger and set slightly higher, the two outer cups close on either side.

38.name: Three dancing figures
38.seen: Three ivory figures in high-belted, flowing classical dresses turn in a loose ring, hair gathered up in carved curls, bare feet mid-step, the ivory threaded with fine gold-brown veins.

38.name: The linking hands
38.seen: Below the raised arms, free hands reach sideways at waist height: the central dancer’s hand rests on the right-hand dancer’s hip, and the left-hand dancer’s open hand reaches toward the central dancer’s side.

38.name: The crescent and two discs
38.seen: High in the upper left of the paler oval sky, a slim silver-grey crescent is carved in relief, with a small round disc on either side of it, left and right.

38.name: The river of stars
38.seen: A glittering diagonal band of silvery flecks runs from the upper right of the dark border down into the lighter oval sky, toward the centre of the card.

38.name: The castle by the water
38.seen: On the right horizon, carved in pale grey-blue lapis, a turreted manor with many windows stands among trees above still water, crossed by an arched stone bridge; a single leafy tree answers it on the left hill.

38.name: The ring of gourds
38.seen: Around the dancers’ feet an oval garland of round pumpkins and long curved gourds, with vine leaves and curling tendrils, is carved in greyish lapis, framing the lower half of the scene.

38.name: Clusters of grapes
38.seen: Several bunches of grapes, carved as tight beaded clusters in blue-grey lapis, sit among the gourds and vine leaves of the garland, the largest at its lower right, below the right-hand dancer’s feet.

39.name: The star-marked fourth cup
39.seen: Held out in mid-air at the upper right, a stemmed cup of grey-blue lapis carries a small gold star with eight slender points on its bowl, the only gold set into any cup on the card.

39.name: The hand from the cloud
39.seen: An ivory hand with a plain cuff at the wrist reaches out of a billowing lapis cloud at the right edge, fingers and thumb closed around the cup’s stem just beneath the bowl.

39.name: The sheltering tree
39.seen: A broad tree carved in pale grey-blue lapis rises at the left, its canopy of narrow pointed leaves arching over the scene; the seated figure leans against its trunk, where thick roots spread into the grass.

39.name: The glittering diagonal band
39.seen: A band of tiny pale, glittering crystals runs diagonally from beneath the tree’s canopy down to the right, fading out above the mountain’s right-hand slope, passing above and right of the figure’s head among gold star flecks.

39.name: The bowed head
39.seen: The ivory figure’s head tilts down and slightly to the right, eyelids lowered, lips closed, short hair carved in soft waves; the gaze falls toward the grass, not up toward the offered cup.

39.name: Arms folded across the chest
39.seen: Both forearms cross over the chest, the fingers of one hand resting on the opposite arm, while the figure sits cross-legged in a long, loose tunic that falls in soft folds, bare feet showing.

39.name: The single blue peak
39.seen: Behind the figure’s shoulder a broad mountain of lighter blue lapis rises to one soft summit, with lower hills running off to the left behind the tree trunk and to the right behind the cups.

39.name: Three cups on the grass
39.seen: Three identical stemmed cups of plain grey-blue lapis stand evenly spaced in a row on the grassy mound, to the right of the figure’s drawn-in feet, in the same grey-blue as the hill behind them.

40.name: The bowed ivory hood
40.seen: A tall figure carved in warm ivory stands wrapped from head to ground in one heavy cloak. The hood is drawn far forward over the face, and the head bends low toward the right.

40.name: Hands held to the chest
