40.seen: The hands are drawn up and gathered at the breast inside the folds of the cloak, just below the hooded chin. Neither hand reaches toward any of the five cups.

40.name: Three fallen cups
40.seen: Three pale grey lapis goblets lie on their sides, one to the left of the figure and two in the foreground, their bowls carved with round, coiled ornament. Thin pale trickles run from the mouths of two of them.

40.name: The gold-hearted cup
40.seen: On a flat rock ledge to the right, a little further back than the figure, a tall goblet stands upright. A small heart of gold is set between two incised bands on its bowl.

40.name: The far cup on the ridge
40.seen: Higher and further away, on the far bank to the left, just behind the figure’s bowed shoulder, a second goblet stands upright: smaller than the gold-hearted cup, carved in the same grey-blue stone, with no gold.

40.name: The arched bridge
40.seen: Behind the figure a small stone bridge with a single rounded arch crosses the river, carved in muted blue lapis. Its far end disappears behind the ivory cloak.

40.name: The castle on the hill
40.seen: On a rocky hill at the right, beyond the river, stands a castle carved in paler lapis: a tall crenellated keep between round towers, one with a pointed roof, and arched doorways at its base.

40.name: Puddles in the stone
40.seen: Across the foreground the lapis ground is marked with shallow, irregular puddle shapes with raised pale rims, gathered around the fallen cups and running down to the bottom edge of the card.

40.name: The Milky Way above
40.seen: A glittering diagonal band of pale mineral runs from the left side of the sky up toward the top centre, among scattered gold star flecks on the deep ultramarine ground.

41.name: The gold Milky Way
41.seen: A diagonal band of glittering gold and pale flecks crosses the sky from the upper left, passing over the carved frame and fading above the garden wall; small stars are carved at the frame’s upper left.

41.name: Gatehouse and garden wall
41.seen: At the upper left a small stone gatehouse with a round-arched doorway stands at the top of a rising path; a long wall of carved blocks closes the garden, with a grove of trees beyond it.

41.name: The guard walking away
41.seen: A small helmeted figure in a short tunic, carved in lapis, walks up the path toward the arch with back turned, a round shield on the left arm and a tall spear in the right hand.

41.name: The cup on the pillar
41.seen: Right of centre a plain round column rises from the garden, carved in lapis and topped by a lapis cup holding a single five-petalled flower with two small leaves.

41.name: The gold-hearted cup
41.seen: The standing figure bends forward and offers a plain ivory goblet with a rounded bowl, short stem and wide foot, holding it in both hands; a gold heart is inlaid on the front of the bowl.

41.name: Open hands below
41.seen: The kneeling figure lifts both hands just beneath the goblet, palms up and fingers spread, not yet touching it, while the face tilts upward toward the taller figure.

41.name: The kneeling child
41.seen: On the right a smaller ivory figure with long hair tied back kneels in a sleeveless gown with a draped sash, looking up toward the taller figure, who stands barefoot and bends down from the left.

41.name: Flowering cups at the edges
41.seen: Four lapis cups stand in pairs down the two sides of the garden, each holding one carved five-petalled flower; with the pillar cup and the ivory goblet they make the card’s six.

41.name: The cracked ivory ledge
41.seen: Both figures rest on one ivory ledge that is cracked across into two pieces: the standing figure’s bare feet on the rougher left piece, the kneeling figure on the smoother right piece.

42.name: The dreamer’s open hands
42.seen: The ivory figure is seen from behind, face turned up in profile toward the cups. The right hand is raised, palm open toward the clouds; the left arm reaches out low to the side, palm open and empty.

42.name: The calm head, far left
42.seen: From the leftmost cup, an ornate bowl carved with scrollwork, rises a serene face with long hair falling to the rim. It looks straight out of the card rather than toward the dreamer.

42.name: The rising serpent
42.seen: From a plain stemmed cup a serpent lifts its body in a tall S-curve, scales finely incised, mouth open with a thin tongue flicking toward the glowing figure in the next cup.

42.name: The veiled figure of light
42.seen: A veiled head and shoulders rise from the third cup, ringed by fine radiating lines of light. On the plain bowl beneath is set a small eight-pointed star of gold, the only gold among the cups.

42.name: Laurel crowning a skull
42.seen: The central cup, set highest of the seven on the crest of the cloud, holds a skull in its bowl, framed by a laurel wreath whose two branches arch up behind it and stay open at the top.

42.name: Heaped jewels and a crown
42.seen: A wide bowl carved with a lily-like emblem is piled high with smooth, rounded jewels, and a small crown rests at the front of the heap, facing the viewer.

42.name: The winged dragon
42.seen: A small cup, set lower than its neighbours just right of the jewels, holds a winged dragon with open jaws and one clawed forefoot raised, its wings spread wide against the dark lapis sky.

42.name: The tower on the crag
42.seen: At the far right a tall square tower with a pointed roof, arched door and narrow windows stands on rocks inside a cup, which is itself perched on a jagged lapis mountain.

42.name: The bank of cloud
42.seen: Five cups stand on a long band of billowing cloud carved in lighter blue lapis. The leftmost cup rests on a low hill with small shrubs, the rightmost on a jagged rocky slope.

43.name: The moon with closed eyes
43.seen: High on the right hangs a full, round moon carved in pale greyish blue lapis. Its face is turned slightly toward the left, eyes closed and lips shut, with small star shapes incised in the sky around it.

43.name: The glittering road overhead
43.seen: A band of glittering pale mineral crosses the dark ultramarine sky diagonally, from the top edge near the centre down toward the left-hand hills, among scattered gold star flecks.

43.name: The hooded ivory traveller
43.seen: The only ivory figure on the card walks away from the viewer, up a rocky path. A hood covers the head and a heavy cloak falls in deep folds to the ankles. The feet are bare, one heel lifted mid-step.

43.name: The long walking staff
43.seen: The traveller grips a long, slender ivory staff in the right hand at chest height, its rounded knob above the hand and its foot planted on the rock just left of the walking feet.

43.name: Bare trees on the slopes
43.seen: Leafless, finely branched trees are carved in low relief on the left-hand slopes and on the rocks to the right of the path, in the same blue lapis as the hills.

43.name: The winding river
43.seen: A river winds out of the hills on the left, runs behind the cups and breaks into white water over rocks at the lower right, between the cups and the traveller’s path.

43.name: The gap in the row
43.seen: The upper row holds three cups on the left and then stops. In the space where more cups could stand, the river and its white water show through the carved rocks.

43.name: Eight cups in two rows
43.seen: Eight stemmed cups, three in the upper row and five in the lower, are carved from the same blue lapis as the ground. All stand upright and unbroken, rims level, lined up close together.

43.name: The gold fish
43.seen: On the leftmost cup of the lower row a small fish in gold relief swims across the bowl, scales and fins detailed, facing right toward the river and the traveller.

44.name: Nine cups in an arc
44.seen: Nine stemmed goblets stand in a shallow arc along a curved ledge, each carved from grey-blue lapis with a fluted lower bowl and a rounded knop on the stem. The row dips lower toward both ends.

44.name: Gold heart on the centre cup
44.seen: The fifth cup, at the peak of the arc and directly above the figure’s head, carries a small inlaid heart of bright gold on its bowl. The other cups show only scattered, irregular gold flecks.

44.name: The draped curved shelf
44.seen: The cups rest on a curved ledge covered with a cloth whose edge falls in swags with a scalloped fringe and small pendant drops, with tassels hanging near each end, all in pale lapis.

44.name: The smiling face and cap
44.seen: The ivory figure’s round face is creased by a broad smile, eyes narrowed almost shut, cheeks full. Short curls show beneath a small rounded cap with a narrow brim.

44.name: Arms folded high
44.seen: Both arms are folded high across the chest in thick, rounded sleeves; the fingers of one hand show against the opposite upper arm. Nothing is held; the cups stand behind the figure, out of reach.

44.name: The knotted rope belt
44.seen: A plain cord circles the waist of the long ivory tunic and ties in a loose knot at the centre, its two ends hanging down over the lap and fraying into small tassels.

44.name: The curtain behind the seat
44.seen: Behind the figure hangs a pale blue lapis curtain gathered in swags beneath the shelf, its side lengths falling to cords that end in tassels level with the figure’s elbows.

44.name: Arched windows on the land
44.seen: Two tall round-arched openings flank the seat. Through the left one, in low relief, a tree stands on a hillside above still water, with a mountain beyond; the right shows rolling slopes and a distant ridge.

44.name: Milky Way above the cups
44.seen: Above the cups a glittering band of pale mineral crosses the dark ultramarine sky diagonally, running from the upper left down toward the row of cups, among scattered small gold stars.

45.name: The gold-heart cup
45.seen: At the very top of the arch, directly above the cottage, one lapis goblet carries a solid gold heart inlaid across its bowl. Five cups descend the arch on either side of it.

45.name: Ten star-marked goblets
45.seen: Ten grey-blue goblets with knopped stems and fluted feet are carved in low relief along the arch, five either side of the heart cup. Each bowl bears a tiny incised star touched with gold.

45.name: The carved stone arch
45.seen: A broad band of paler, greyer lapis rises from the left near the figures’ raised hands, curves in a near semicircle above the cottage and comes down on the right, framing the valley like a window.

45.name: The cottage in the valley
45.seen: Inside the arch, a small cottage with a thick thatched roof, a single chimney and a few dark windows sits on a low rise, carved in muted blue lapis among rolling hills.

45.name: The broad tree and cypresses
45.seen: To the left of the cottage stands one broad, full-crowned tree on a slender trunk; to its right rise two tall, narrow cypresses side by side, their tips reaching into the starry sky.

45.name: The embracing pair
45.seen: Two barefoot ivory adults stand pressed together: a bearded figure with cloth at the hips wraps one arm round the waist of a veiled figure in a long robe. Each lifts one open hand skyward.

45.name: The dancing children
45.seen: To the right, two smaller ivory children hold hands mid-dance, knees bent, heels lifted, each raising the free arm. The curly-haired one laughs openly; the taller, long-haired one tips the face upward.

45.name: The cascade and stream
45.seen: On the far left, a small waterfall spills over carved rocks into a pool beside the adults. Inside the arch on the right, a winding stream drops over a little fall of its own.

45.name: The glittering mineral vein
45.seen: From the left edge beside the figures, a pale band of glittering mineral runs diagonally down toward the lower centre of the dark lapis, among scattered gold star flecks and fine hairline cracks.

46.name: The gold fish
46.seen: A fish of burnished gold rises head first from the ivory bowl, its round eye and scales finely worked, mouth open, side fins just above the rim, its head tilted up toward the bending face.

46.name: The plain ivory bowl
46.seen: The cup is a simple, deep ivory bowl with a smooth rim and no stem, held at chest height; both hands support it from below, the fingers of the nearer hand spread across its base.

46.name: The smiling, lowered face
46.seen: Carved in ivory near profile, the head bows toward the bowl, eyes lowered and nearly closed, lips curved in a quiet smile, soft curls massed at the side of the head beneath the cap.

46.name: The plumed cap
46.seen: A rounded ivory cap with a rolled band sits low on the curls; a long, finely barbed feather springs from its top and curls back over the head toward the left.

46.name: The river of stars
46.seen: A pale band of silvery sparkle crosses the upper lapis sky diagonally, from near the top edge down toward the left, among scattered gold flecks, a few of them with tiny pointed rays like small stars.

46.name: The lotus-patterned tunic
46.seen: The knee-length ivory tunic, gathered at the waist by a narrow belt and finished with a patterned hem band, is scattered with small incised fan-shaped sprays that resemble budding lotus flowers.

46.name: The carved waves
46.seen: Behind the figure, rows of long rippling waves are cut in lighter blue lapis across the full width of the card, above a rough rocky shore and a floor of diagonal planks.

46.name: The tiered fountain
46.seen: At the left, carved in lighter blue stone against the waves, stands a small fountain: a wide round basin, two smaller stacked bowls rising above it and a bud-shaped finial at the top.

46.name: The lotus and the shrub
46.seen: On the right, just above the rocky shore, a single open lotus flower on a short stem is carved in blue lapis, with a small rounded shrub or tree beside it.

47.name: The river of stars
47.seen: A long diagonal band of glittering pyrite specks crosses the night sky from near the top edge, right of centre, down to the left, passing above and left of the raised cup before fading over the hills.

47.name: Winged helmet, head bowed
47.seen: The rider’s rounded ivory helmet has a brim, a guard framing the face and two small feathered wings rising from the crown; the face, in three-quarter view, looks down, not up at the cup.

47.name: Goblet on the open palm
47.seen: An ivory goblet with a knopped stem rests on the flat of the rider’s outstretched hand, raised high above the horse’s bowed head; a single gold fish is inlaid on the bowl.

47.name: Armour under soft cloth
47.seen: Beneath the loose ivory tunic the rider wears plate armour: a rounded shoulder piece, a jointed elbow guard on the rein arm and a knee guard above a greave on the visible leg.

47.name: The blue horse, head lowered
47.seen: Carved in lighter, greyer lapis rather than ivory, the horse bows its head deeply, mane cut in flowing strands; a bridle crosses its face and a broad rein patterned with leafy scrolls runs back to the rider’s low hand.

47.name: Fish on cloth and tunic
47.seen: Small fish are carved along a lapis band crossing the horse’s flank and on the square saddlecloth beside it; fainter fish are scattered across the rider’s long ivory tunic, some tilted as if swimming.

47.name: The winged heel
47.seen: The rider’s foot, in a pointed ivory shoe fastened with a strap at the ankle, carries a small feathered wing at the heel, where a spur would usually sit.

47.name: The raised foreleg
47.seen: The horse’s near foreleg is lifted and bent at the knee, hoof hanging above the ground near the water’s edge, while the other three legs stand on the rocky bank.

47.name: Stream and a row of stones
47.seen: A stream winds from the far hills across the left of the scene towards the horse’s raised hoof, with a row of rounded stones lying across it just ahead; trees stand on the banks beyond.

48.name: The covered cup
48.seen: An ivory cup with a domed, leaf-carved lid, a spired finial and a fluted lower bowl; two winged figures form its handles, their bodies tapering into curled tails. One hand grips the stem, the other cradles the foot.

48.name: The gold heart
48.seen: A small heart of gold is set into the smooth upper band of the bowl, just below the lid and facing the viewer; apart from the flecks in the sky, it is the only gold on the card.

48.name: The bowed head
48.seen: The Queen’s head bends toward the cup, eyelids lowered and mouth closed; long wavy hair falls over the shoulders, and a mantle is knotted at the throat above a gown tied at the waist.

48.name: The cross-tipped crown
48.seen: An open ivory crown rests on the Queen’s hair, its band edged with small beads and its tall points tipped with little trefoil crosses, carved in the same pale material as the figure and the cup.

48.name: The scallop-shell throne
48.seen: Behind the Queen, a tall throne carved in lighter blue lapis rises to a rounded arch filled by a large scallop shell, with a smaller shell at its base and two small cherubs perched on the arch.

48.name: Cherubs on the throne base
48.seen: On the lower panel of the throne, carved in blue lapis, a plump winged cherub faces the viewer and reaches one arm up the frame, while a second small head peeps out behind it; leafy scrolls fill the panel.

48.name: Crescent and sky shells
48.seen: At upper left, a thin crescent moon is carved in pale lapis, with small scallop shells floating beside and below it in the sky, above low carved clouds and the flat line of the sea.

48.name: Gold stars in the night
48.seen: Gold flecks are scattered across the deep ultramarine sky, a few larger ones rayed like small stars; a glittering diagonal vein crosses the upper sky from the top right down toward the left edge.

48.name: The pebbled shore
48.seen: The Queen sits on a low shelf of rounded, polished pebbles; water curls around its left edge in carved ripples, a bare foot shows beneath the hem, and sea plants grow at lower right.

49.name: The gold fish pendant
49.seen: A small gold fish, its body covered in fine carved scales, hangs head up from a thin gold chain at the centre of the chest; fish and chain are the only gold on the ivory figure.

49.name: The ivory cup, held level
49.seen: The hand on the viewer’s left grips the stem of a plain ivory goblet with a deep, rounded bowl, a knop on the stem and a flared foot, holding it upright at chest height, close to the body.

49.name: The lotus-topped sceptre
49.seen: The other hand grips a short, slender ivory sceptre near its lower end; the shaft rises to a small collar and ends in a carved flower head of layered, pointed petals, like a lotus bud.

49.name: The ivory crown
49.seen: An ivory crown with a decorated band and upright points ending in small trefoils, the tallest at the front centre, rests on long, wavy ivory hair; it is carved plain, without gold.

49.name: The scrolled blue throne
49.seen: A throne carved in paler, greyer lapis rises behind the King, its arched back ending in spiral scrolls at both upper corners; the armrests and square side posts carry shallow carved panels.

49.name: The leaping fish
49.seen: At the left, a large scaled fish carved in grey-blue lapis arcs up out of the waves, tail still in the water, mouth open and head turned towards the throne.

49.name: The sailing ship
49.seen: On the right, a tall ship with full, bellied sails and a pennant at the top of its highest mast rides the waves; raised decks and fine rigging lines are cut into the grey-blue lapis.

49.name: The round stepped dais
49.seen: The throne stands on a round lapis plinth of two stepped tiers, pale blue and finely cracked, its lower edge lapped by carved waves; the King’s ivory feet rest on the upper tier.

49.name: The rolling waves
49.seen: A broad band of sea in deep and pale blue lapis crosses the lower card, its crests curling into small spirals that break against the dais, above a plain dark lapis margin.

50.name: The hand from the cloud
50.seen: A carved ivory hand emerges from a billowing ivory cloud, its wrist vanishing into the cloud on the right, its fist closed round the bound grip, thumb folded over the fingers, holding the sword vertically.

50.name: The blade pointing down
50.seen: Below a three-lobed pommel and a crossguard whose ends curl into round scrolls, the long ivory blade hangs point downward, a fine central ridge running to its sharp tip above the mountains.

50.name: The gold crown on the blade
50.seen: An open circlet of gold, the one large piece of gold on this card, is threaded onto the blade below the crossguard; the ring is seen in perspective, and its points end in small beads, the central point taller than the rest.

50.name: The palm frond, left
50.seen: On the viewer’s left a long palm frond, carved in paler grey-blue lapis, sweeps up and outward from a stem that ends beside the blade just below the crown, its fine leaflets angled toward its tip.

50.name: The olive branch, right
50.seen: On the right an olive sprig in the same pale lapis rises from beside the blade toward the upper right, with slender pointed leaves and small round olives along its stem, mirroring the palm across the sword.

50.name: Five falling blue drops
50.seen: Five teardrop shapes in smooth, pale blue lapis hang in the air below the branches, three to the left of the blade and two to the right, each pointed at the top and rounded below.

50.name: A glittering band of stars
50.seen: At mid-left a diagonal vein of pale, sparkling mineral crosses the dark lapis like a band of stars, while gold flecks, one larger and star-shaped near the upper left, are scattered across the whole sky.

50.name: Twin peaks in lapis
50.seen: Two steep, faceted peaks rise in the lower third in lighter blue lapis, with smaller ridges at either edge and a level horizon behind; the sword’s tip points into the gap between them.

50.name: Travellers in the valley
50.seen: Between the peaks, tiny low-relief figures in muted blue: a hooded, robed walker beside a four-legged animal, and a fainter figure higher up the left-hand slope behind them.

51.name: The ivory blindfold
51.seen: A broad band of ivory is wrapped flat across the seated figure’s eyes. Long wavy hair, parted in the centre, falls to the shoulders; the mouth is closed and the face is level and calm.

51.name: Two curving ivory swords
51.seen: Two long ivory swords rise from the shoulders and bend outward like sabres, each ending in a small round knob. Each lower shaft carries two short crossbars before slanting down beneath the hands.

51.name: The gold crescent moon
51.seen: A slender crescent of gold hangs in the upper right, above the right-hand sword, its horns opening to the left. Small gold flecks scatter through the dark lapis sky around it.

51.name: Arms crossed at the breast
51.seen: The bare forearms cross over the chest, and each open hand lies flat against the opposite upper arm, fingers together. The hands grip nothing; the swords slip beneath them.

51.name: The medallion over the heart
51.seen: A round raised disc sits on the breast of the gown, its lower edge meeting the crossed wrists, its face carved with concentric rings. The two sword shafts converge toward it.

51.name: The sea behind the seat
51.seen: Behind the figure a band of lighter blue lapis is carved as sea, its straight horizon at shoulder height and its surface scored with fine horizontal ripples from edge to edge of the scene.

51.name: Rocky islets with caves
51.seen: Small craggy islets of grey-blue lapis rise from the water on both sides, three on the left and two on the right, each hollowed at its base by one or two dark arched openings.

51.name: The plain stone bench
51.seen: The figure sits upright on a simple bench of pale grey-blue lapis, a flat slab on square legs, set on a low pale ledge. Beneath the draped gown both bare feet rest side by side.

51.name: A glittering vein below
51.seen: From just beneath the ledge a diagonal vein of pale, sparkling mineral runs down toward the lower left across the dark lapis, catching light in tiny blue and white points.

52.name: The carved ivory heart
52.seen: An anatomical heart carved in ivory, not a stylised valentine: the great vessels rise from its top, its chambers swell in soft relief, and all three blades meet inside it.

52.name: Gold seams across the heart
52.seen: Thin rivers of gold run over the ivory heart, pooling on its upper left shoulder and branching down through its centre like veins or mended cracks.

52.name: The upright centre sword
52.seen: The central ivory sword stands exactly vertical, its flared, fluted pommel and bound grip high among the clouds, its crossguard ending in rounded knobs, its blade driving straight down into the heart.

52.name: Two slanting side swords
52.seen: Two matching ivory swords lean inward from left and right, their pommels roughly level with the centre sword’s crossguard, their blades entering the heart’s upper shoulders on either side of the vessels.

52.name: Three points below
52.seen: Beneath the heart three clean, pale points fan out. The side blades cross inside the heart, so the left-hand sword’s point emerges lower right, the right-hand sword’s lower left; the centre point drops straight down.

52.name: Storm clouds in grey lapis
52.seen: Heavy, billowing clouds carved in lighter greyish blue lapis bank behind the hilts across the upper half of the card, and reach down on both sides to the level of the heart.

52.name: Slanting incised rain
52.seen: Fine pale lines are scratched into the lapis below the cloud line, slanting from upper right to lower left and filling both sides of the lower card around the blade points.

52.name: Glittering vein and gold flecks
52.seen: In the upper left a diagonal vein of pale, glittering mineral crosses the dark lapis like a thread of stars, while small gold flecks sit near all four corners of the card.

53.name: The gold devotional niche
53.seen: High in the centre, a pointed niche holds the card’s only gold figures: a haloed standing figure holding an open book and a cross-topped staff, and a smaller figure kneeling before it, palms pressed together.

53.name: The glittering night vein
53.seen: Across the upper left a diagonal band of pale, sparkling mineral runs through the dark lapis, and small gold stars are scattered above the arches and below the tomb.

53.name: Two pointed Gothic arches
53.seen: Carved in paler lapis, two pointed arches with ribbed vaults stand left and right on slender clustered columns with leafy capitals; small arched windows are cut into their side walls.

53.name: Three swords on the wall
53.seen: Three lapis swords lie horizontally one above another across the back wall, points to the left, hilts to the right with disc pommels and straight crossguards; the lowest is set furthest right.

53.name: The sleeping ivory knight
53.seen: An ivory effigy in full plate armour lies on its back, head on a cushion at the left, long hair spread, eyes closed, hands joined palm to palm on the chest.

53.name: The ivory sword alongside
53.seen: An ivory sword lies along the front edge of the slab: pommel beyond the cushion, curled crossguard just below the head, blade running beneath the bent arm. A shorter sheathed blade hangs at the hip.

53.name: The lion at the feet
53.seen: At the right end of the slab a small maned ivory lion lies with forepaws stretched out and head turned toward the viewer, the effigy’s pointed armoured feet resting just above it.

53.name: The sword on the tomb
53.seen: Carved in lapis along the front of the tomb chest, a long sword lies horizontally with its disc pommel and crossguard at the left and its point toward the right.

53.name: Ten hooded mourners
53.seen: Below the tomb sword a frieze of hooded, robed figures with hands joined runs along the chest in two groups of five, each group turned toward the centre, a gap between them.

54.name: The smile over the shoulder
54.seen: The ivory figure in the foreground has close curls and a calm profile. The head turns back toward the two figures behind, and the mouth lifts in a small, pleased smile.

54.name: Two swords hugged close
54.seen: Two ivory swords are clasped diagonally against the chest by one crossed arm, blades rising past the shoulder to just above the horizon, hilts low on the chest at the viewer’s left: one crossguard and two round pommels.

54.name: The sword held point down
54.seen: In the other hand, on the right of the card, a third sword with a lobed pommel hangs point down and outward, gripped just below the crossguard, its tip reaching almost to the lower corner of the relief.

54.name: Two blades on the stones
54.seen: Two ivory swords lie parallel on the blue lapis rocks at the lower left, points toward the card’s edge, crossguards and round pommels to the right, close to the hem of the foreground figure’s robe.

54.name: The face hidden from view
54.seen: The farther of the two figures behind, in a short belted tunic and soft boots, bends forward on the rocky slope, one arm raised and a hand pressed over the face.

54.name: The bowed figure
54.seen: Nearer the foreground, a second figure in a matching tunic walks toward the cliffs with head sunk low, arms hanging loose and empty at the sides, the back heel lifted mid-step on the rocks.

54.name: The carved sea
54.seen: Behind all three figures a sea carved in rippled blue lapis stretches to a straight horizon, its small waves incised as fine pale lines across the middle of the card.

54.name: Gold clouds torn apart
54.seen: High in the dark lapis sky, ragged streaks of gold stretch sideways like clouds pulled apart by wind, with small gold four-pointed stars scattered around them.

54.name: A glittering diagonal vein
54.seen: A pale vein of glittering mineral runs diagonally through the lapis, from beneath the right end of the gold clouds down toward the cliffs above the two figures behind, like a trail of fine stars.

55.name: Six upright ivory swords
55.seen: Six ivory swords stand in a close row in the left half of the boat, points hidden inside the hull, hilts rising above the passengers: knobbed pommels, straight crossguards, plain blades, the row fanning slightly apart.

55.name: The hooded passenger and child
55.seen: In the middle of the boat a seated figure, wrapped from head to knee in a hooded mantle, bows over a curly-haired child and holds the child close with both arms. The child’s face turns towards the viewer.

55.name: The figure at the pole
55.seen: At the right end of the boat a barefoot figure in a long tunic and wrapped headcloth leans forward towards the passengers, one raised hand gripping the top of a long pole that slants down past the stern into the water behind.

55.name: The ivory boat in choppy water
55.seen: A plain, long, shallow ivory boat with a raised prow at the left and a small crossbar near the stern. Pale-crested waves ripple around its hull; with the pole pushing back to the right, it travels left.

55.name: The gilded far shore
55.seen: Beyond the boat the water lies flat and finely lined. Across it, a low bank of rounded lapis trees runs the width of the card, and a thin vein of gold traces the waterline along most of its length.

55.name: Sun-face and crescent together
55.seen: At the upper right a pale grey-blue disc with a calm, open-eyed face sends out long, straight rays; at the upper left a thin crescent moon curves in lighter lapis. Gold flecks glitter in a diagonal band below them.

55.name: Wolves beneath the sun
55.seen: Below the sun a seated wolf lifts its muzzle towards the rayed face. Lower down, two more wolves with bushy tails stand facing each other on the far bank, all carved in grey-blue lapis.

55.name: The dog on the rock
55.seen: At the lower left a large seated dog in grey-blue lapis, tall pointed ears raised and mouth closed, sits upright on a rocky ledge at the water’s edge and faces the prow of the boat.

55.name: The crayfish below
55.seen: Beneath the waves, on dark rocky ground, a grey-blue crayfish lies angled from lower left to upper right, both claws held out and long antennae arching overhead; a small rounded stone lies to the left of its tail.

56.name: The sidelong smiling glance
56.seen: The ivory figure’s curly head turns three-quarters toward the viewer, lips curved in a small, knowing smile, eyes glancing sideways out of the card while the body keeps moving to the left.

56.name: The armful of swords
56.seen: Above the shoulder three ivory hilts with ball pommels and crossguards rise among three bare, upturned points; below the forward arm, three blade ends slant downward, one greyer than the rest. The bundle crosses the back diagonally.

56.name: The outstretched open hand
56.seen: The forward arm swings out to the left, fingers spread and loosely curled, the open hand hovering in the direction of the two planted swords. The other arm bends behind the back, its hand resting at the waist with fingers loosely curled.

56.name: Two swords left planted
56.seen: Two grey-blue swords carved in the lapis itself stand point-down in the ground on the left, side by side, with ball pommels and flared crossguards. Cracks in the stone run through the ground beneath them.

56.name: Soldiers at the campfire
56.seen: On the right, four small figures carved in grey-blue lapis gather round a fire flickering with gold: two stand, a third leans in just behind the flames, a fourth sits in front. All four face the fire.

56.name: The gold pennant
56.seen: A swallow-tailed pennant of glittering gold streams to the right from a slender pole with a knob at its tip, set on the peak of the largest tent. It is the largest patch of gold on the card.

56.name: The tents of the camp
56.seen: Four peaked tents in lighter blue lapis stretch across the middle of the card. The largest has a scalloped valance; one is cut off at the left edge, another stands behind the fireside group.

56.name: The Milky Way overhead
56.seen: A broad diagonal band of pale, glittering mineral crosses the upper lapis sky from the upper left toward the lower right, with scattered gold flecks like stars above the tents.

56.name: Feet on tiptoe
56.seen: Both bare feet point left, a thin band at the front ankle. The rear foot rises high on its toes, heel lifted, while the front foot touches down toes first on the uneven lapis ground.

57.name: The gold blindfold
57.seen: A wide band of textured gold covers the eyes and wraps around the head, set into the ivory like gold leaf. The head bows forward and a little to the viewer’s left; the mouth is calm.

57.name: Four blades on the left
57.seen: Four dark blue swords carved in the lapis stand point-down in the ground on the viewer’s left, each with a round pommel and a straight crossguard, leaning at slightly different angles and heights.

57.name: Five blades on the right
57.seen: Five more swords of the same dark lapis stand on the viewer’s right against the rocky slope, at staggered heights. Nine blades in all flank the figure; none touches it, and none stands in front.

57.name: The loosely knotted sash
57.seen: A long ivory sash wraps under the chest and around the arm on the viewer’s right, crosses the gown diagonally, loops into a loose knot at the right hip and trails a frayed end.

57.name: The free hand
57.seen: On the viewer’s left the arm hangs down at the side, and the ivory hand rests against the gown at thigh level, fingers relaxed. The other arm bends back behind the body, wrapped by the sash.

57.name: The castle on the crag
57.seen: High on the right, a many-towered castle carved in paler blue lapis crowns a steep, fissured crag whose slope falls away behind the swords on the viewer’s right.

57.name: The river of stars
57.seen: A diagonal drift of pale, glittering specks crosses the dark sky from the upper left down toward the crag and the bowed head, with small gold stars scattered separately across the sky.

57.name: Pools in cracked ground
57.seen: The foreground is carved as cracked plates of lighter lapis broken by shallow, darker, polished hollows like standing water. The bare ivory feet stand on a paler patch between them.

58.name: Hands over the face
58.seen: The ivory figure’s head is bowed forward into the palms; long fingers spread across brow and eyes so that no face can be seen, and wavy hair falls loose down the back.

58.name: Eight carved lapis swords
58.seen: Eight swords, counted blade by blade, lie horizontally one above another across a tall panel, carved in pale grey-blue lapis, every point aimed left. None touches the figure; the lowest passes behind the bowed head.

58.name: Staggered hilts and pommels
58.seen: On the right the crossguards and round pommels do not line up: each hilt sits a little further in or out than its neighbour, and several round pommels jut past the panel’s right edge onto the starry lapis.

58.name: The tall panelled wall
58.seen: Behind the bed rises a tall panel carved in the lapis, crowned with a moulded cornice and set with recessed frames, like a shut door or shutter; the swords are mounted across it.

58.name: Sitting up in bed
58.seen: The figure sits upright among the bedclothes in a loose ivory gown with gathered long sleeves, torso slumped forward over the quilt, one forearm lying slack across it with the hand hanging loose.

58.name: The single gold rose
58.seen: On the quilt, a little below the hanging hand, one rose is inlaid in gold with a short stem and two leaves. It is the only gold anywhere on the bed or bedclothes.

58.name: A quilt of carved roses
58.seen: The lighter blue quilt spills over the bed’s edge in heavy folds, stitched into a diamond lattice with a small carved rose in every compartment, repeated across the whole cover.

58.name: The carved duel
58.seen: On the bed’s end panel at lower left, two small figures in tunics are carved in low relief, one swinging a sword overhead, the other stepping in with a raised blade.

58.name: Gold stars beyond the panel
58.seen: Small gold flecks and a few tiny starbursts are scattered across the dark lapis around the panel and the bed, from the top corners down to the lower edge.

59.name: Nine lapis swords
59.seen: A close row of swords carved in greyish blue lapis, not ivory, stands upright above the figure’s back. Counted carefully there are nine, each with a round ball pommel, a straight crossguard and a groove down the blade.

59.name: Blades along the spine
59.seen: The blades enter the ivory back in an even line from the lower back to the shoulders. The middle blades stand almost straight while the outermost lean slightly outward. No blood is carved anywhere.

59.name: The resting face
59.seen: The ivory head, with short curled hair, lies turned toward the viewer, the cheek pillowed on the crook of a folded arm. The eyes are closed; brow and mouth are relaxed.

59.name: Two extended fingers
59.seen: At the end of the long outstretched arm, the ivory hand rests on the rock with the index and middle fingers extended and held apart, the remaining fingers curled in toward the palm.

59.name: The ivory drapery
59.seen: A thin ivory cloth covers the hips and legs in soft, deep folds and spills over the rock. The back, shoulders and arms are bare; the covered legs run to the card’s left edge.

59.name: Gold dawn on the horizon
59.seen: Behind the figure a calm sea runs flat to a straight horizon. On the right a thin band of gold light lies along the horizon line, with fainter gold glints reflected on the water below it.

59.name: Low bank of clouds
59.seen: Heavy, billowing clouds carved in lighter greyish blue lapis fill the middle band of the card behind the sword hilts, rising highest on the left and thinning toward the horizon on the right.

59.name: A sky full of stars
59.seen: Most of the upper card is open night: scattered gold flecks, a pale glittering band running diagonally from the upper right toward the centre, and one brighter rayed star on the right.

59.name: The lapis rock ledge
59.seen: The figure lies on a broad, flat ledge of rough, bright blue lapis, its surface chipped and textured with lighter veins, dropping away to darker, cracked stone along the bottom of the card.

60.name: The ivory sword, gold hilt
60.seen: A long, straight ivory blade with a faint central ridge slants up and to the right into the night sky. The crossguard and round pommel are gold; one hand grips above the crossguard, the other below it.

60.name: The turned head
60.seen: While the body is seen partly from behind, the ivory head turns into profile towards the viewer’s right, the gaze directed past the gripping hands. Short hair is tossed out on both sides by the wind.

60.name: The Milky Way and stars
60.seen: A glittering band of pale flecks crosses the lapis sky diagonally from the upper left towards the lower right, passing behind the upper blade. Small gold points of pyrite are scattered around it.

60.name: Windswept clouds
60.seen: Clouds carved in paler, greyer lapis gather on the upper left, their lower edges pulled out into long horizontal streaks, as though dragged sideways by a strong wind.

60.name: The scattered birds
60.seen: Small pale birds with outstretched wings, carved in light lapis, fly in a loose trail across the sky above the trees on the left, with a few more on the right near the horizon.

60.name: Wind-bent trees
60.seen: A stand of slender trees grows on a hill at the left edge, carved in pale blue lapis, their thin trunks leaning and their feathery crowns tossed by the wind.

60.name: The distant pinnacle
60.seen: On the right horizon a single tall, narrow rock pinnacle rises from a plateau carved in low relief, standing apart from the flatter hills and plains around it.

60.name: Bare feet on rock
60.seen: Both feet are bare. The back foot touches the rock only with its toes, heel lifted; the front foot is planted flat on rough, broken lapis. Fine thread-like strands wrap around both lower legs.

60.name: Spirals in the stone
60.seen: Two concentric spirals are incised into the boulders at the lower left, like ancient rock carvings; the lower one is larger, with more turns, and the upper sits on a rounded stone.

61.name: The raised gilded sword
61.seen: A long, straight gold blade with a central groove, raised high above the rider’s head and angled back toward the upper right; its crossguard with knobbed ends, grip and round pommel are ivory.

61.name: The helmeted, leaning rider
61.seen: An ivory figure in a rounded helmet, face in profile, leans over the horse’s neck, one fist on the reins, the other lifting the sword. From the waist down the armour is lapis, a scabbard hanging at the hip.

61.name: The cloak streaming back
61.seen: A heavy ivory cloak flies out behind the rider’s shoulders in long folds, its end curling open toward the right edge, between the two banks of wind-torn cloud.

61.name: Horse of ivory and lapis
61.seen: The horse’s head, neck, mane and chest are ivory; from the shoulder the stone turns to blue lapis for body, legs and tail. Its mouth is open around the bit, both forelegs bent and lifted clear of the ground.

61.name: Butterflies and birds on the chest
61.seen: On the lapis of the horse’s chest, just below a thin raised line curving across it, sit four small pale grey reliefs in a row: butterfly, bird, butterfly, bird, all with wings open.

61.name: Three birds in flight
61.seen: Three small birds carved in pale grey-blue lapis cross the sky with wings spread: two to the left of the raised arm, one to the right, just below the line of the blade.

61.name: Wind-torn clouds
61.seen: Two banks of greyish-blue clouds are carved along the right side of the card, stretched into long horizontal streaks with ragged edges, as though dragged across the sky by a strong wind.

61.name: Bare trees bent by wind
61.seen: Leafless trees in lighter blue lapis lean hard, their branches swept toward the right; the one below the horse grips the sloping ground with spread, exposed roots. The rider gallops the other way, toward the left.

61.name: Glittering vein across the sky
61.seen: A long diagonal band of tiny pale, glittering mineral specks crosses the dark lapis from the upper right toward the left, high above the sword, among scattered gold star flecks.

62.name: The upright ivory sword
62.seen: A long, straight ivory blade stands vertical at arm’s length ahead of the Queen’s face, its point rising higher than the crown; a closed fist grips it below a crossguard with a raised centre and flared ends, above a round pommel.

62.name: Crown of gold butterflies
62.seen: The Queen, in profile facing left, wears a gold-rimmed crown whose points are gold butterflies, one large at the front and smaller ones beside it, over curling ivory hair gathered at the nape.

62.name: Open hand, tasselled cord
62.seen: The other arm reaches forward at shoulder height, palm open and fingers raised; a knotted ivory cord is tied loosely around the wrist, its long end hanging down to a tassel.

62.name: The child’s head crest
62.seen: A curly-haired child’s head carved in pale lapis crowns the top of the throne back, shown in profile and looking left, the same way as the Queen; no wings are visible.

62.name: Butterflies on the throne
62.seen: Several butterflies of different sizes are carved in shallow relief on the tall lapis throne back, scattered behind the Queen’s crown, head and shoulders; another rests on the side panel below the armrest.

62.name: The lone bird
62.seen: A single bird with outspread wings flies in the open night to the right of the throne, carved in grey-blue lapis, heading left towards the Queen’s back.

62.name: The glittering diagonal band
62.seen: A band of fine sparkling flecks crosses the deep blue sky diagonally from the top edge above the throne down towards the left, passing behind the upper blade; gold stars are scattered around it.

62.name: Wind-bent trees
62.seen: A stand of slender trees at the lower right is carved in dark lapis, their crowns blown sharply to the left and their trunks curving under the force of the wind.

62.name: Clouds beneath the throne
62.seen: Heaped cumulus clouds carved in lapis fill the bottom of the card, rising around the ivory hem and the throne’s square legs; smaller clouds are cut into the blue cloak draped over the armrest.

63.name: The drawn ivory sword
63.seen: A long ivory blade rises from the King’s right fist, leaning slightly towards the viewer’s left; the crossguard has a raised, ornamented centre and rounded flared ends, and a small carved pommel shows beneath the fist.

63.name: Gold star at the tip
63.seen: Where the blade would normally narrow to a point, it ends instead in a small round cap set with a gold eight-pointed star, the one gold accent on the ivory figure and its sword.

63.name: The ivory crown
63.seen: The King, seated full-face and looking straight out of the card, wears an open ivory crown of pointed, knobbed tips over long hair; its band is carved with small ornament and the tallest tip stands at the centre.

63.name: The hand at rest
63.seen: The King’s other hand lies on the lap near the knee, over the ivory robe, palm down with the fingers together and gently curved, while the sword hand stays closed around the grip beside it.

63.name: Six lapis butterflies
63.seen: Six butterflies carved in pale grey-blue lapis are arranged in mirrored pairs inside the wreath: two beside the upper crescent, two larger ones level with the King’s head, and two small ones lower down.

63.name: Four gold crescents
63.seen: Three pale gold crescent moons are set along the top block of the throne, the central one largest; a fourth crescent hangs inside the wreath directly above the crown.

63.name: The leafy wreath
63.seen: A wide ring of overlapping pointed leaves, carved in lapis in low relief, encircles the King’s head and upper body against the throne back, enclosing all six butterflies and the fourth crescent.

63.name: Twin cypresses
63.seen: Two tall, narrow cypresses carved in lighter blue lapis rise behind the upper corners of the throne, each with a smaller tree beside it, framing the open sky above the crest.

63.name: Two birds in flight
63.seen: Between the cypresses, two birds carved in grey-blue lapis fly one behind and below the other, wings raised, in the open strip of night sky above the throne’s crescent-topped crest.

64.name: The ivory disc and gold star
64.seen: A thick, plain ivory disc with a raised rim around a slightly recessed face rests on the open palm; near its centre sits one small five-pointed star of gold.

64.name: The open palm
64.seen: A large ivory hand, palm upward, reaches in from the right with its wrist bare; the fingers extend relaxed past the disc’s left edge, and nothing closes over the disc, which rests on the palm ungripped.

64.name: The cloud at the edge
64.seen: A dense bank of ivory cloud, carved in soft rounded masses with lapis showing through its gaps, fills the right edge; the wrist emerges from it and wisps trail left beneath the hand.

64.name: The trail of stars
64.seen: A narrow diagonal band of glittering silver specks crosses the upper left sky, running from near the top left corner down toward the hand, among scattered gold flecks and fine cracks in the stone.

64.name: The path to the mountains
64.seen: Carved in pale lapis, a narrow path winds from the hedge arch back through low hills toward a range of mountains with one peak higher than the rest.

64.name: The crenellated towers
64.seen: Square towers of pale blue lapis, with stepped crenellations and visible courses of stone, rise at the left and right edges of the garden; a crenellated wall runs back into the hills from the left tower.

64.name: The lilies on the left
64.seen: Tall lilies with open, star-shaped blooms and long pointed leaves stand in a cluster on the left, carved in lighter blue lapis and rising above the top of the hedge.

64.name: The roses on the right
64.seen: Full, many-petalled roses among serrated leaves fill the bed on the right, carved in lighter lapis just above the hedge line and beside the right-hand tower.

64.name: The arch in the hedge
64.seen: A low, dense hedge of textured lapis crosses the foreground; at its centre it rises into a rounded arch wreathed with small carved roses, and the path passes through its opening.

65.name: The gold-hearted pentacle
65.seen: An ivory disc carved with a five-pointed star rests upright on the open palm of the raised arm, high at the upper right; the centre of the star is filled with gold.

65.name: The glittering diagonal band
65.seen: A band of fine sparkling flecks runs diagonally across the dark blue sky, from the top edge down towards the left, above and behind the figure’s head; small gold stars are scattered across the field around it.

65.name: Soft cap, lowered eyes
65.seen: The head tilts down to the left under a soft ivory cap with a drooping point; loose curls frame a calm face whose eyes are lowered or closed, not watching either disc.

65.name: The looping ribbon
65.seen: A long, flat ivory ribbon loops up behind the raised pentacle, crosses the lifted forearm, swings out behind the back to the left of the body and curls down beside the lower disc, making several open loops against the sky.

65.name: The plain disc at the waist
65.seen: A second ivory pentacle, carved with a star but with no gold, is held low at the right of the body by a hand reaching across the waist, the ribbon curling close beside it.

65.name: Two ships on high waves
65.seen: Behind the figure a rough sea of curling crests is carved in lighter blue lapis; a large ship under full square sails rides on the left, and a smaller ship with a great curved sail pitches on the right.

65.name: Chained winged figures
65.seen: A horned, bat-winged creature with a curling tail, carved in blue lapis, stands at each side, face turned up; each grips a fine chain, cuffed at its wrist, rising to the figure’s knee or tunic hem.

65.name: One foot on the ridge
65.seen: Below the waves rises a range of sharp lapis mountains; one foot, in a soft slipper with an ankle strap, rests on a glittering saddle between two peaks while the other foot is lifted, knee bent.

65.name: The castle among the peaks
65.seen: At the bottom centre, directly beneath the dancer, a walled castle with many slender spired towers is carved in pale lapis, set into the mountain range between the two winged figures.

66.name: The gold pentacle above
66.seen: At the apex of the pointed arch, inside a moulded circle, a solid five-pointed star is inlaid in gold; it is the only gold on the carved architecture and sits above the other two.

66.name: Two lapis pentacles
66.seen: Lower left and lower right of the gold star, two pentagrams are cut into the lapis inside raised circles of matching size, drawn in outline with their inner lines and left in the stone’s own blue.

66.name: The carved five-petalled flower
66.seen: Between the two lower pentacles and directly beneath the gold one, a single five-petalled flower with a round centre and small leaves at either side is carved in the lapis of the arch.

66.name: The Gothic doorway
66.seen: A tall pointed arch, carved in pale lapis, rests on clustered columns with carved capitals; within its inner arch a church façade with spires, tracery windows and a statue in a niche is cut in shallow relief.

66.name: Hammer and chisel
66.seen: The curly-haired ivory worker raises a block-headed hammer in one hand and sets a chisel against the wall with the other; fine cracks run through the lapis around the chisel’s point.

66.name: The tonsured figure’s joined hands
66.seen: On the left, a figure in an ivory monastic habit with a tonsured head looks up at the worker, palms pressed together at the chest; a lowered hood lies around the shoulders.

66.name: The hooded onlooker
66.seen: On the right, a figure in a long ivory robe with the hood raised over the head looks up at the worker in profile, holding the right corner of the open sheet at chest height.

66.name: The plan held open
66.seen: A broad, blank ivory sheet is held open by its upper corners between the two onlookers, hanging in front of the worker’s waist and thighs; nothing is drawn on its visible face.

66.name: The carved bench
66.seen: The worker stands on a low ivory bench whose front opens in an arch with three carved tracery panels above it; a folded cloth lies on its top beneath the feet.

67.name: The walled city behind
67.seen: Carved in paler lapis on the horizon, a walled city of crowded roofs and pointed towers rises to one tall keep with a conical roof; crenellated walls and an arched gate face the plain, a low hill to the left.

67.name: The star above the crown
67.seen: A five-pointed star carved in pale blue lapis, with no disc around it, hangs just above the tallest point of the crown, separated from it by a narrow gap, against the foot of the city walls.

67.name: The crown and level gaze
67.seen: An ivory crown of pointed tines, the tallest at the centre, sits on thick waves of hair; below it a bearded face looks straight out with drawn brows and a closed, unsmiling mouth.

67.name: The gold star on the disc
67.seen: Pressed flat against the chest, a large plain ivory disc carries a five-pointed star inlaid in textured gold, the only large piece of gold on the card; elsewhere gold appears as small flecks and tiny stars in the sky.

67.name: Hands clasped beneath the disc
67.seen: Both ivory hands meet at the lower rim of the disc, one folded over the other, the forearms curving in from either side so that the arms form a closed ring around it against the body.

67.name: The squared ivory block
67.seen: The figure sits on a plain rectangular block of rough ivory, visible on both sides of the robe, with squared edges and a pitted, unornamented surface; the robe falls over its front to the ground.

67.name: The star at the left
67.seen: On the pale lapis ground to the left of the seat stands a bevelled, five-pointed blue star, upright and apart from the figure; the ivory foot nearest to it rests on bare ground.

67.name: The star at the right
67.seen: A matching bevelled blue star stands on the ground to the right of the seat, mirroring the left one, so that with the star overhead the three lapis stars frame the figure in a wide triangle.

68.name: The gold star above
68.seen: At the crown of the window’s tracery, a solid five-pointed star inlaid in gold sits inside a carved roundel. Apart from small flecks in the night sky, it is the only gold on the card, set high above both figures.

68.name: Five pentacles in stone
68.seen: Below the gold star, five pentagrams inside circles are carved in the lapis itself, arranged as a pair, then one, then another pair, all in the same cold blue as the wall.

68.name: The unlit Gothic window
68.seen: A tall pointed arch frames tracery shaped as a bare, leafless tree rising from a single trunk, with the pentacles held in its branches. No light shows through, and pale snow lines the sill.

68.name: The shawled walker
68.seen: A figure in warm cream ivory, shawl drawn over the head, walks to the right with head bowed and eyes cast down; both arms fold across the chest, one hand gripping the shawl.

68.name: The bowed, hooded head
68.seen: Behind, on the left, a second figure in greyer, weathered ivory hunches forward under a deep hood, face shadowed and turned down towards the snow, a torn cloak trailing from the shoulders.

68.name: The dark house
68.seen: At the right edge, a small building is carved in shadowed lapis, its pitched roof edged with snow and its walls faintly marked; no lit window shows anywhere on it.

68.name: The two crutches
68.seen: The hooded figure leans on two pale crutches with plain crossbars under the arms; both hands grip the handles halfway down, and the tips press into the snow on either side of the body.

68.name: The bandaged foot
68.seen: The one foot visible beneath the ragged trouser leg is bound in wrapped strips of cloth up to the shin, and steps forward into the snow between the two crutch tips.

68.name: Bare feet, footprints
68.seen: The shawled figure walks barefoot over pale, frosted lapis; small hollow footprints are pressed into the snow behind and between the walkers, and a few low stones break the surface near the bottom edge.

69.name: Five pentacles in the sky
69.seen: Five round lapis discs, each with a raised rim and a carved five-pointed star, form an arch over the giver’s head: one at the top, two higher at the sides, two lower.

69.name: The glittering diagonal band
69.seen: A band of fine pale sparkling flecks runs diagonally across the dark lapis from the lower left towards the upper right, passing between the carved pentacles; small gold stars are scattered around it.

69.name: Crenellated walls and tower
69.seen: Behind the figures, a battlemented town wall is carved in paler lapis across the card; on the left it rises into a square tower with a small window, and the wall continues on the right.

69.name: The raised balance scales
69.seen: The giver’s left hand holds a pair of scales by the top of its upright pointer, at shoulder height; two shallow, empty ivory pans hang on cords from a beam that is close to level.

69.name: The sword at the hip
69.seen: A sword hilt carved in grey-blue stone, with a round pommel and a slanted crossguard, shows at the giver’s left hip beside the nearer scale pan; a short length of blade runs down along the robe.

69.name: The giver’s lowered hand
69.seen: The giver’s right hand reaches down and outwards from a wide sleeve with an embroidered cuff, fingers pointing down and loosely curled, directly above the gold pentacle; the giver’s gaze is lowered towards it.

69.name: The gold-starred pentacle
69.seen: A sixth disc, paler grey-blue with a raised rim, carries a five-pointed star inlaid in gold; it hangs in the air between the giver’s hand and the upturned palms below.

69.name: The hooded kneeler
69.seen: On the right, a figure in a hooded cloak kneels with face turned up towards the giver; both hands are raised, fingers spread and empty, close to the giver’s robe; a bare foot shows behind.

69.name: The cupped, upturned palms
69.seen: On the left, a barefoot figure in a ragged tunic with a torn hem, head bound with a cloth band, kneels on one knee and holds both palms cupped together beneath the gold pentacle.

70.name: The gilded top pentacle
70.seen: At the crown of the bush, higher than every other disc, one grey-blue pentacle carries a five-pointed star outlined and partly filled in gold; the six discs below it show only incised stars.

70.name: Five plain discs
70.seen: Five grey-blue discs, each incised with an outlined pentagram, sit at different heights among the branches, clustered near the top and trailing down the right side of the bush.

70.name: The upturned gaze
70.seen: The curly-haired ivory figure tilts the head back, chin propped on the hands, and lifts the eyes up and to the right, towards the higher discs and the top of the bush.

70.name: Hands folded on the handle
70.seen: Both hands are stacked on the top end of the long ivory handle, and the figure’s chin rests on them, so the weight of the upper body leans onto the tool.

70.name: The long-handled spade
70.seen: An ivory spade with a long straight shaft runs diagonally from the figure’s hands down to the right; its flat blade, narrowing to a blunt point, is set into the soil beside the bush.

70.name: The tall pale-blue bush
70.seen: A branching bush carved in lighter lapis rises from the soil at the right to above the figure’s head, its stems covered in deeply cut, serrated leaves; a smaller sprig grows behind the figure’s back.

70.name: The disc at the root
70.seen: The seventh pentacle sits low at the base of the bush, almost on the soil, framed by leaves a short distance to the right of the spade blade.

70.name: Tilled soil and seedlings
70.seen: The whole lower band is dug soil carved in rough, furrowed lapis; the figure stands on it barefoot, and tiny seedlings are cut into the ground along the bottom edge.

70.name: The river of stars
70.seen: A band of fine glittering flecks crosses the night sky diagonally from the top edge down towards the left, among scattered gold stars, on the side away from the figure’s gaze.

71.name: The gold star in progress
71.seen: On the bench top lies an ivory disc whose five-pointed star is inlaid in gold; one hand sets a chisel against the star while the other raises a small square-headed hammer above it.

71.name: The bowed head
71.seen: The craftsperson, carved in ivory with close curls, leans far forward on the bench, head bowed and eyes lowered to the disc; the sleeves are rolled and an apron is tied at the back with a bow.

71.name: Seven pentacles on the pillar
71.seen: Seven finished ivory pentacles hang from small pegs down a square pillar of paler lapis beside the bench, five along its left edge and two staggered to the right; each star is cut in outline, not gold.

71.name: Two pentacles set down
71.seen: At the lower left an ivory pentacle leans against the bench’s left leg on the rocky ground; a second leans against the bench’s right leg, both with outlined stars and no gold.

71.name: The moon with a face
71.seen: High in the star-flecked sky a pale lapis disc carries a calm face with lowered eyes, edged on the left by a thin ivory crescent; a glittering diagonal band crosses the sky below it.

71.name: The harbour town
71.seen: At the left, carved in greyed lapis, a walled town with a tall spired tower rises from the water’s edge before a range of mountains; a single-masted sailboat floats on the bay below.

71.name: Two columns at the shore
71.seen: Two plain round columns with simple capitals stand on rocks at the water’s edge in the middle distance, framing the bay between them; both are carved in greyed lapis like the hills behind them.

71.name: The howling pair
71.seen: Two canines sit on rocky ledges either side of the columns, muzzles raised to the sky: a smooth-coated, dog-like animal on the left and a shaggy wolf with a bushy tail on the right.

71.name: The crayfish in the shallows
71.seen: Between the two animals a crayfish lies in the rippled water near the shore, its head and claws turned to the left and its long antennae arching above, carved in shallow relief in the same blue as the waves.

72.name: The hooded falcon
72.seen: An ivory falcon perches on the raised hand at left, talons gripping a fitted glove with a flared cuff. A small hood with a loop on top covers its head; its long tail hangs down beside the wrist.

72.name: The bare hand on the grapes
72.seen: The other hand hangs ungloved at right, fingertips resting lightly on the vine stem just above a heavy cluster of grapes. The veiled head is bowed, eyes lowered, looking at neither bird nor fruit.

72.name: Nine grey-blue discs
72.seen: Counted disc by disc, nine grey-blue lapis pentacles with incised five-pointed stars sit among the vine leaves: six stacked beside the gown at left, three spaced down the right edge.

72.name: A tenth disc in gold
72.seen: Just below the grape cluster at right, one further disc carries a five-pointed star inlaid in gold, the only gilded pentacle on the card. With it, the discs number ten.

72.name: The flowered ivory gown
72.seen: The figure wears a long ivory gown with a deep V neck, a sash at the high waist and full elbow-length sleeves, carved all over with small flower sprays; a veil drapes over the head, long hair falling beneath it.

72.name: The manor among trees
72.seen: Far off at upper right, a gabled manor house with tall chimneys and mullioned windows is carved in pale blue lapis, sheltered by tall trees on softly rolling ground.

72.name: The glittering Milky Way
72.seen: A broad diagonal band of crushed, sparkling fragments, silver and pale blue, runs from the top centre down towards the left horizon, among scattered gold star flecks in the dark lapis sky.

72.name: The small snail
72.seen: On the bare ground just below the hem, a small snail with a spiralled shell is carved in pale grey stone, horns raised, moving towards the right.

73.name: Discs framing the arch
73.seen: Nine grey-blue discs, each carved with a line-drawn pentagram, frame the archway: one above its point and four stacked down each side, the lowest left one half hidden by the elder. Two more sit against the robe, eleven in all.

73.name: The glittering starry band
73.seen: A diagonal band of fine sparkling flecks runs from beside the top disc down to the left, between the upper discs and past the left shoulder of the arch; small gold stars dot the surrounding blue.

73.name: The arch of shields
73.seen: A pointed Gothic arch carved in paler grey-blue lapis rises over the couple on two masonry pillars. Five heraldic shields are set into its band, a rampant lion on the central one, with fleur-de-lis finials along the outer edge.

73.name: The couple under the arch
73.seen: Two standing figures carved in blue lapis face each other beneath the arch: one curly-haired, a cloak pinned at the shoulder; one veiled, in a long gown, an open hand raised mid-gesture.

73.name: The ivory elder
73.seen: The only ivory figure on the card sits at the lower left in profile, long wavy hair falling over the shoulders and a full beard down the chest, gazing right towards the couple.

73.name: Moons and grapes on the robe
73.seen: The elder’s ivory mantle is covered in fine relief: crescent moons near the shoulder, clusters of grapes and winding vine scrollwork across drapery that pools down to the ground.

73.name: The child and the dog
73.seen: At the right, beside the arch’s right pillar, a curly-haired child in a tunic, carved in lapis, rests one hand on the head of a slender standing dog and raises the other; the dog faces left, towards the elder.

73.name: The seated greyhound
73.seen: A greyhound-like dog carved in blue lapis sits at the elder’s knee, facing right, head raised beneath a resting ivory hand, its long tail curling on the ground; a second dog stands at the right beside the child.

73.name: The gold pentacle
73.seen: Low against the robe, near the hem, a lapis disc bears a solid five-pointed star of worked gold, the only gilded emblem on the card; a grey disc with a line-drawn pentagram rests higher, against the elder’s lap.

74.name: The river of gold flecks
74.seen: Across the dark lapis sky, a diagonal band of dense gold flecks, with a few paler specks over a faint haze, runs from the upper right down towards the left, ending just left of the raised disc.

74.name: The ivory disc
74.seen: A thick ivory disc with a raised rim, held at eye level; a five-pointed star is incised in thin lines within an inner circle, and only a small solid star at its centre is gold.

74.name: Two hands, two jobs
74.seen: The ivory hand further from the viewer cups the disc from below, palm up; the nearer hand rests along its side with fingers spread, steadying it rather than gripping.

74.name: The level, absorbed gaze
74.seen: The head is carved in clean profile, facing left, with short tight curls and no hat; the eyes look straight across at the disc, lips closed, face calm and unhurried.

74.name: The grove on the left
74.seen: Behind the figure and to the left, a grove of rounded trees is carved in pale lapis relief on the horizon, one taller tree with a slender, forked trunk standing in front.

74.name: A single distant peak
74.seen: On the right, low hills rise to one broad peak carved in greyer lapis, with a thin band of cloud above it; it sits far behind the figure, at the level of the waist.

74.name: The classical ivory drape
74.seen: A thin garment clings to the chest, leaving the arms bare; below it, heavier cloth is gathered in a roll at the waist and falls in deep vertical folds to the calves.

74.name: The ploughed field
74.seen: Across the left half of the ground and up behind the feet, many parallel furrows sweep in long curving arcs, carved in ridged lapis that catches the light along each crest.

74.name: Bare feet in the grass
74.seen: Both ivory feet are bare and planted on grass carved with small tufts; one is set ahead of the other, heels down, in a slow step towards the left.

75.name: The pentacle on an open palm
75.seen: An ivory disc inlaid with a gold five-pointed star, drawn in a double line, rests upright on the rider’s flat, upturned palm, held out at chest height toward the horse’s head.

75.name: The lowered visor
75.seen: The rider’s rounded ivory helmet has its visor lowered over the eyes, leaving nose, mouth and chin bare above a collar of fine mail; the face is in profile, turned toward the disc.

75.name: Oak sprigs, helmet and bridle
75.seen: A sprig of lobed ivory oak leaves rises from the crest of the helmet; a matching sprig in a paler, greyer tone is tucked into the horse’s headstall just in front of its ears.

75.name: Reins held low and loose
75.seen: The rider’s other ivory hand rests at waist height, just above the saddle, holding thin blue reins that sag in a soft curve along the neck to the bit.

75.name: The heavy, standing horse
75.seen: A thick-necked, broad-bodied horse carved in mottled lapis stands side-on facing left, ears pricked; all four hooves rest flat on the furrows and its long tail hangs straight down.

75.name: Armoured leg and spur
75.seen: Below the ivory skirt, in front of a plain square saddle cloth, the rider’s leg shows mail at the thigh, then plate from knee to pointed foot; a small spur juts from the heel.

75.name: The farmhouse at the field’s edge
75.seen: On the far left, beyond the furrows, a gabled farmhouse with a chimney, small windows and wide double doors stands in pale lapis among leafy trees, two to its left and one to its right.

75.name: The ploughed furrows
75.seen: Deep, regular furrows carved in the lapis curve across the whole lower third of the card, ridge after ridge, with finer rows rolling back toward the hills; the horse stands directly on them.

75.name: Crossing veins of light
75.seen: Two diagonal bands of tiny glittering mineral specks cross high in the dark lapis sky, up and to the left of the rider, forming a loose X among scattered round gold star flecks.

76.name: The rose arbour
76.seen: A lapis rose vine climbs from both sides of the throne and meets in an arch above it, carved with open roses, tight buds and serrated leaves in paler blue relief against the starred night.

76.name: Two winged cherubs
76.seen: Two cherub heads with small feathered wings nestle in the rose vine, one on each side of the arch; the left one looks down, the right one turns its round face out towards the viewer.

76.name: The goat’s head crest
76.seen: A lapis goat’s head with ridged, backward-curving horns and a short beard crowns the top of the throne back, midway between the two pear-topped posts and just above the Queen’s crown.

76.name: Pears on the throne posts
76.seen: Two plump carved pears sit on top of each throne post, four in all, their stalks upright; the posts beneath them are cut with fine scrollwork in the same greyed lapis as the throne.

76.name: Ivory crown, lowered gaze
76.seen: The Queen wears a low ivory crown with small points over long wavy hair drawn forward over one shoulder; the head tilts down and the eyes rest on the disc in the lap.

76.name: The gold pentacle
76.seen: An ivory disc rests in the Queen’s lap, cradled by both hands, one beneath it and one at its edge; a gold five-pointed star of interlaced lines is inlaid on it, its field flecked with gold.

76.name: River through the valley
76.seen: Beyond the right arm of the throne a river winds out of a valley between wooded slopes, below a peaked mountain; more hills rise on the left behind the throne, all carved in soft lapis.

76.name: The leaping rabbit
76.seen: A grey-blue rabbit carved in lapis stretches in mid-leap across the grass at the lower left, ears raised, facing the ivory hem of the Queen’s gown.

76.name: Berry plants underfoot
76.seen: The ground around the throne is dense with carved foliage: broad-leaved plants and stems heavy with round berries fill the foreground on both sides of the ivory hem and the two shoe tips.

77.name: The lapis castle
77.seen: A castle carved in greyed lapis fills the space behind the throne: crenellated walls, conical-roofed towers and small arched windows rise from the King’s shoulders to well above the laurel wreath.

77.name: The laurel wreath
77.seen: In place of a crown, a wreath of pointed ivory laurel leaves circles the King’s head above long wavy hair; the calm face looks straight out at the viewer.

77.name: Four bulls’ heads
77.seen: Four horned bulls’ heads carved in blue lapis project from the throne: two at the top corners of its back at shoulder height, two lower at the front corners of the seat, level with the King’s knees.

77.name: The ivory sceptre
77.seen: The King’s right hand, on the viewer’s left, holds an ivory sceptre by its shaft, angled up past the shoulder; it ends in a knobbed, three-lobed finial above a ringed collar, with a rounded knob below the fist.

77.name: Robe carved with grapes
77.seen: The ivory robe is carved with bunches of grapes, vine leaves and tendrils down the front and along the hem, with a band of flowers and a central rosette across the shoulders.

77.name: The gold pentacle
77.seen: An ivory disc with a raised rim stands upright on the King’s lap at the left side, on the viewer’s right; a gold five-pointed star with incised inner lines is inlaid on it, and the left hand rests along its top edge.

77.name: The vine underfoot
77.seen: A lapis grapevine spreads across the raised ground beneath the throne, heavy with grape clusters and broad lobed leaves; tendrils climb both sides of the seat, and one sandalled ivory foot rests on the vine-covered ground.
